verses.1:1: These are the names of the sons of Israel who came into Egypt together with Jacob their father; each one of them entered with his whole household:
verses.1:4: Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.
verses.1:5: Now Joseph was in Egypt; and all the souls who came from Jacob were seventy-five.
verses.1:6: And Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation.
verses.1:7: But the children of Israel increased and multiplied, and became a teeming throng, and grew exceedingly mighty; and the land multiplied them.
verses.1:8: Now another king arose over Egypt, who did not know Joseph.
verses.1:9: And he said to his nation, "Behold, the race of the children of Israel is a great multitude, and is stronger than we;
verses.1:10: come, therefore, let us deal craftily with them, lest they multiply, and when war happens to us, these also will be joined to our adversaries, and having waged war against us, they will go out from the land."
verses.1:11: Therefore he set overseers of labors over them, that they might afflict them in their labors; and they built fortified cities for Pharaoh, namely Pithom and Raamses and On, which is Heliopolis.
verses.1:12: Yet the more they humbled them, so much the more numerous they became, and they grew exceedingly mighty; and the Egyptians abhorred the children of Israel.
verses.1:13: And the Egyptians oppressed the children of Israel by force,
verses.1:14: and they made their life grievous in hard labors, in clay and in brickmaking, and in all the labors in the fields, in all the works with which they enslaved them with force.
verses.1:15: Then the king of the Egyptians spoke to the midwives of the Hebrews, to the one whose name was Shiphrah, and the name of the second was Puah;
verses.1:16: and he said, "When you serve as midwives to the Hebrew women and they are about to give birth, if it is a male, slay him; but if it is a female, preserve her alive."
verses.1:17: But the midwives feared God, and did not do as the king of Egypt commanded them, and they kept the male children alive.
verses.1:18: So the king of Egypt called the midwives and said to them, "Why is it that you have done this thing, and have kept the male children alive?"
verses.1:19: And the midwives said to Pharaoh, "The Hebrew women are not like the women of Egypt, for they give birth before the midwives come in to them, and they gave birth."
verses.1:20: Therefore God dealt well with the midwives, and the people multiplied and grew exceedingly strong.
verses.1:21: Because the midwives feared God, they made houses for themselves.
verses.1:22: Then Pharaoh commanded all his people, saying, "Every male that is born to the Hebrews, cast into the river, and every female, keep alive."
verses.2:1: Now there was a certain man of the tribe of Levi who took one of the daughters of Levi.
verses.2:2: And she conceived and bore a male child; and seeing that he was fair, they hid him three months.
verses.2:3: And when they could no longer hide him, his mother took a basket for him and coated it with bitumen and pitch, and placed the child in it, and set it in the marsh by the river.
verses.2:4: And his sister kept watch from afar to learn what would happen to him.
verses.2:5: Then the daughter of Pharaoh came down to bathe at the river, and her maidservants walked along beside the river; and seeing the basket in the marsh, she sent her maidservant and took it up.
verses.2:6: And when she opened it, she saw a child weeping in the basket; and the daughter of Pharaoh took pity on him, and said, "This is one of the children of the Hebrews."
verses.2:7: Then his sister said to the daughter of Pharaoh, "Do you wish that I call for you a nursing woman from among the Hebrews, that she may nurse the child for you?"
verses.2:8: And the daughter of Pharaoh said to her, "Go." So the young maiden went and called the mother of the child.
verses.2:9: And the daughter of Pharaoh said to her, "Keep this child safely for me and nurse him for me, and I will give you your wages." So the woman took the child and nursed him.
verses.2:10: And when the child had grown, she brought him in to the daughter of Pharaoh, and he became a son to her; and she called his name Moses, saying, "Out of the water I took him up."
verses.2:11: Now it came to pass in those many days, when Moses had grown to manhood, that he went out to his brethren, the children of Israel. And observing their toil, he saw an Egyptian man striking a certain Hebrew, one of his own brethren of the children of Israel.
verses.2:12: And looking around this way and that, he saw no one; and having struck down the Egyptian, he hid him in the sand.
verses.2:13: And going out on the second day, he saw two Hebrew men fighting with one another, and he said to the one doing wrong, "Why do you strike your neighbor?"
verses.2:14: And he said, "Who appointed you ruler and judge over us? Do you intend to slay me in the manner you slew the Egyptian yesterday?" Then Moses feared and said, "Has this matter indeed become so openly known?"
verses.2:15: Now Pharaoh heard this matter, and sought to slay Moses; but Moses withdrew from the presence of Pharaoh and dwelt in the land of Midian; and when he came into the land of Midian, he sat down by the well.
verses.2:16: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters, who tended the sheep of their father Jethro; and coming there, they drew water until they filled the troughs, to water the sheep of their father Jethro.
verses.2:17: And the shepherds came and drove them away; but Moses rose up and delivered them, and drew water for them, and watered their sheep.
verses.2:18: Then they came to Reuel their father; and he said to them, "Why have you made haste to return today?"
verses.2:19: And they said, "An Egyptian man delivered us from the shepherds, and also drew water for us and watered our sheep."
verses.2:20: And he said to his daughters, "And where is he? Why have you left the man behind? Call him, therefore, that he may eat bread."
verses.2:21: And Moses took up his abode with the man; and he gave Zipporah his daughter to Moses as a wife.
verses.2:22: And the woman conceived and bore a son; and Moses called his name Gershom, saying, "Because I am a sojourner in a strange land."
verses.2:23: Now after those many days, the king of Egypt died; and the children of Israel groaned because of their labors and cried out, and their cry went up to God because of their labors.
verses.2:24: And God heard their groaning, and God remembered His covenant with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob.
verses.2:25: And God looked upon the children of Israel, and He was made known to them.
verses.3:1: Now Moses was tending the sheep of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian; and he led the sheep beyond the wilderness and came to Mount Horeb.
verses.3:2: And the Angel of the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire out of the bush; and he saw that the bush was burning with fire, yet the bush was not being consumed.
verses.3:3: Then Moses said, "I will turn aside and see this great sight, why the bush is not consumed."
verses.3:4: And when the Lord saw that he drew near to look, the Lord called him out of the bush, saying, "Moses, Moses!" And he said, "What is it?"
verses.3:5: And He said, "Do not draw near here; loose the sandal from your feet, for the place on which you stand is holy ground."
verses.3:6: And He said, "I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob." And Moses turned away his face, for he was reverently afraid to gaze before God.
verses.3:7: And the Lord said to Moses, "I have surely seen the affliction of My people who are in Egypt, and I have heard their outcry because of the taskmasters; for I know their anguish;
verses.3:8: and I have come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them out of that land, and to bring them into a good and spacious land, into a land flowing with milk and honey, into the place of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Girgashites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
verses.3:9: And now, behold, the outcry of the children of Israel has come to Me, and I have seen the oppression with which the Egyptians oppress them.
verses.3:10: And now come, let Me send you to Pharaoh king of Egypt, and you shall bring My people, the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt."
verses.3:11: And Moses said to God, "Who am I that I should go to Pharaoh king of Egypt, and that I should bring the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt?"
verses.3:12: And God spoke to Moses, saying, "Certainly I will be with you; and this shall be the sign to you that I shall send you forth: when you have brought My people out of Egypt, you shall serve God on this mountain."
verses.3:13: Then Moses said to God, "Behold, I shall go out to the children of Israel and say to them, 'The God of our fathers has sent me to you.' And they will ask me, 'What is His name?' What shall I say to them?"
verses.3:14: And God spoke to Moses, saying, "I am He who is." And He said, "Thus you shall say to the children of Israel, 'He who is has sent me to you.'"
verses.3:15: And God said again to Moses, "Thus you shall say to the children of Israel, 'The Lord, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you.' This is My everlasting name, and a memorial to generations of generations.
verses.3:16: Go, therefore, gather the council of elders of the children of Israel, and you shall say to them, 'The Lord, the God of your fathers, has appeared to me, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, saying, "I have surely visited you and looked upon all that has happened to you in Egypt."
verses.3:17: And He said, "I will bring you up out of the affliction of the Egyptians into the land of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Girgashites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, into a land flowing with milk and honey."'
verses.3:18: And they will listen to your voice; and you and the council of elders of Israel shall go in to Pharaoh king of Egypt, and you shall say to him, 'The God of the Hebrews has summoned us; let us therefore go a journey of three days into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to our God.'
verses.3:19: Yet I know that Pharaoh king of Egypt will not let you go, except by a mighty hand;
verses.3:20: and stretching out My hand, I will strike the Egyptians with all My wonders which I will perform among them, and after these things he will send you forth.
verses.3:21: And I will give favor to this people in the sight of the Egyptians; and when you depart in haste, you shall not go away empty-handed:
verses.3:22: each woman shall ask of her neighbor and of the woman dwelling in her house for articles of silver and gold, and for clothing, and you shall put them upon your sons and upon your daughters; and plunder the Egyptians."
verses.4:1: Then Moses answered and said, "If they do not believe me nor listen to my voice—for they will say, 'God has not appeared to you'—what shall I say to them?"
verses.4:2: And the Lord said to him, "What is this that is in your hand?" And he said, "A staff."
verses.4:3: And He said, "Cast it upon the ground." So he cast it upon the ground, and it became a serpent; and Moses fled from it.
verses.4:4: And the Lord said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand and take hold of its tail." So stretching out his hand, he took hold of its tail, and it became a staff in his hand—
verses.4:5: "that they may believe you, that the God of their fathers, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob, has appeared to you."
verses.4:6: And the Lord said to him again, "Put your hand into your bosom." So he put his hand into his bosom; and he brought his hand out of his bosom, and his hand became like snow.
verses.4:7: And He said again, "Put your hand into your bosom." And he put his hand into his bosom; and he brought it out of his bosom, and it was restored again to the color of its flesh.
verses.4:8: "Now if they do not believe you nor listen to the voice of the first sign, they will believe you at the voice of the latter sign.
verses.4:9: And it shall be, if they do not believe you in these two signs nor listen to your voice, that you shall take from the water of the river and pour it out upon the dry ground; and the water that you take from the river shall be blood upon the dry ground."
verses.4:10: Then Moses said to the Lord, "I pray, Lord, I am not capable—neither before yesterday nor before the third day, nor since You began to speak to Your servant; I am weak-voiced and slow of tongue."
verses.4:11: And the Lord said to Moses, "Who has given man a mouth, and who makes the hard of hearing and the mute, the seeing and the blind? Is it not I, God?
verses.4:12: Now therefore go, and I will open your mouth, and I will instruct you in what you are to speak."
verses.4:13: And Moses said, "I pray, Lord, appoint another capable one whom You will send."
verses.4:14: Then the Lord was kindled with wrath against Moses and said, "Is there not Aaron your brother, the Levite? I know that he will surely speak for you; and behold, he himself will come out to meet you, and when he sees you, he will rejoice within himself.
verses.4:15: And you shall speak to him and put My words into his mouth; and I will open your mouth and his mouth, and I will instruct you in what you shall do.
verses.4:16: And he shall speak for you to the people, and he shall be your mouth; and you shall be to him in the things pertaining to God.
verses.4:17: And this staff that was turned into a serpent you shall take in your hand, with which you shall perform the signs."
verses.4:18: Then Moses went and returned to Jethro his father-in-law, and said, "I will go and return to my brethren who are in Egypt, and see whether they are still alive." And Jethro said to Moses, "Go in good health." Now after those many days, the king of Egypt died.
verses.4:19: And the Lord said to Moses in Midian, "Go, depart to Egypt; for all those who were seeking your life have died."
verses.4:20: So Moses took his wife and his children, set them upon the beasts of burden, and returned to Egypt; and Moses took the staff from God in his hand.
verses.4:21: And the Lord said to Moses, "As you go and return to Egypt, see to all the wonders that I have put in your hands, that you perform them before Pharaoh; yet I will harden his heart, and he will by no means send the people away.
verses.4:22: And you shall say to Pharaoh, 'Thus says the Lord: Israel is My firstborn son;
verses.4:23: and I said to you, Send My people away that they may serve Me; now if you are unwilling to send them away, see then, I will slay your firstborn son.'"
verses.4:24: Now it came to pass on the way, at the lodging place, that an angel of the Lord met him and sought to kill him.
verses.4:25: Then Zipporah took a stone and circumcised the foreskin of her son, and fell down at his feet and said, "The blood of the circumcision of my child has ceased."
verses.4:26: And he departed from him, because she had said, "The blood of the circumcision of my child has ceased."
verses.4:27: Now the Lord said to Aaron, "Go into the wilderness to meet Moses." So he went and met him at the mountain of God, and they kissed one another.
verses.4:28: And Moses reported to Aaron all the words of the Lord that He had sent, and all the sayings that He had commanded him.
verses.4:29: Then Moses and Aaron went and gathered together the council of elders of the sons of Israel.
verses.4:30: And Aaron spoke all these words that God had spoken to Moses, and he performed the signs before the people.
verses.4:31: So the people believed, and rejoiced that God had visited the sons of Israel and that He had seen their affliction; and the people bowed down and worshiped.
verses.5:1: And after these things Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh and said to him, "Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, 'Send My people away, that they may hold a feast to Me in the wilderness.'"
verses.5:2: And Pharaoh said, "Who is He whose voice I should listen to, so as to send away the sons of Israel? I do not know the Lord, and I will not send Israel away."
verses.5:3: And they said to him, "The God of the Hebrews has summoned us; therefore we will go a journey of three days into the wilderness, so that we may sacrifice to our God, lest death or slaughter meet us."
verses.5:4: And the king of Egypt said to them, "Why, Moses and Aaron, do you turn my people away from their labors? Depart, each of you, to his labors."
verses.5:5: And Pharaoh said, "Behold, now the people are numerous; let us not therefore give them rest from their labors."
verses.5:6: So Pharaoh commanded the taskmasters of the people and the scribes, saying,
verses.5:7: "Straw shall no longer be given to the people for brickmaking, as yesterday and the third day; let them go themselves and gather straw for themselves.
verses.5:8: And the quota of brickmaking that they make each day you shall lay upon them; you shall take away nothing. For they are idle; therefore they cry out, saying, 'Let us arise and sacrifice to our God.'
verses.5:9: Let the labors of these men be made heavy, and let them concern themselves with these things, and let them not concern themselves with empty words."
verses.5:10: Then the taskmasters and the scribes pressed them hard, and spoke to the people, saying, "Thus says Pharaoh: 'I will no longer give you straw;
verses.5:11: go yourselves and gather straw for yourselves wherever you may find it, for nothing is taken away from your quota.'"
verses.5:12: So the people were scattered throughout all the land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.
verses.5:13: And the taskmasters pressed them hard, saying, "Fulfill your appointed labors each day, just as when straw was given to you."
verses.5:14: And the scribes of the lineage of the sons of Israel, who had been set over them by Pharaoh's overseers, were scourged, and they said, "Why have you not fulfilled your quotas of brickmaking, as yesterday and the third day, and that of today?"
verses.5:15: Then the scribes of the sons of Israel came in and cried out to Pharaoh, saying, "Why do you deal thus with your servants?
verses.5:16: Straw is not given to your servants, yet they tell us to make bricks; and behold, your servants have been scourged. You will therefore wrong your own people."
verses.5:17: And he said to them, "You are idle, you are idlers! Therefore you say, 'Let us go, let us sacrifice to our God.'
verses.5:18: Now therefore go and work; for straw shall not be given to you, yet you shall deliver the quota of brickmaking."
verses.5:19: And the scribes of the sons of Israel saw themselves in distress, when it was said, "You shall not fall short of the daily allotment of brickmaking."
verses.5:20: And they met Moses and Aaron coming to meet them as they came out from Pharaoh,
verses.5:21: and said to them, "May God look upon you and judge, because you have made our odor detestable before Pharaoh and before his servants, putting a sword into his hands to slay us."
verses.5:22: Then Moses returned to the Lord and said, "I pray, Lord, why have You afflicted this people? And why have You sent me?
verses.5:23: For ever since I went to Pharaoh to speak in Your name, he has afflicted this people, and You have not delivered Your people."
verses.6:1: And the Lord said to Moses, "Now you shall see what I will do to Pharaoh; for by a mighty hand he will send them away, and by an uplifted arm he will cast them out from his land."
verses.6:2: Now God spoke to Moses and said to him, "I am the Lord.
verses.6:3: And I appeared to Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, being their God, yet My name, the Lord, I did not make known to them.
verses.6:4: And I established My covenant with them, so as to give to them the land of the Canaanites, the land in which they have sojourned, upon which they also sojourned.
verses.6:5: And I have heard the groaning of the sons of Israel, whom the Egyptians hold in bondage, and I have remembered your covenant.
verses.6:6: Go, speak to the sons of Israel, saying, 'I am the Lord, and I will bring you out from the dominion of the Egyptians, and I will deliver you from bondage, and I will redeem you with an uplifted arm and with great judgment.
verses.6:7: And I will take you to Myself as a people for Me, and I will be your God; and you shall know that I am the Lord your God, who brought you out from the oppression of the Egyptians.
verses.6:8: And I will lead you forth into the land toward which I stretched out My hand to give it to Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, and I will give it to you as an inheritance: I am the Lord.'"
verses.6:9: So Moses spoke thus to the sons of Israel; yet they did not listen to Moses, because of their faintness of spirit and because of the harsh labors.
verses.6:10: Then the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.6:11: "Go in, speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt, that he send away the sons of Israel out of his land."
verses.6:12: But Moses spoke before the Lord, saying, "Behold, the sons of Israel have not listened to me, and how will Pharaoh listen to me? For I am lacking in speech."
verses.6:13: And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, and gave them a charge to Pharaoh king of Egypt, so as to send forth the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt.
verses.6:14: And these are the heads of their fathers' houses. The sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel: Hanoch and Pallu, Hezron and Carmi; this is the kindred of Reuben.
verses.6:15: And the sons of Simeon: Jemuel and Jamin and Ohad and Jachin and Zohar, and Shaul, the son of the Phoenician woman; these are the paternal families of the sons of Simeon.
verses.6:16: And these are the names of the sons of Levi according to their kindreds: Gershon and Kohath and Merari; and the years of the life of Levi were one hundred and thirty-seven.
verses.6:17: And these are the sons of Gershon: Libni and Shimei, the houses of their paternal family.
verses.6:18: And the sons of Kohath: Amram and Issachar, Hebron and Uzziel; and the years of the life of Kohath were one hundred and thirty years.
verses.6:19: And the sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. These are the houses of the paternal families of Levi according to their kindred.
verses.6:20: And Amram took Jochebed, the daughter of his father's brother, to himself as a wife, and she bore to him Aaron and Moses and Miriam their sister; and the years of the life of Amram were one hundred and thirty-two years.
verses.6:21: And the sons of Izhar: Korah and Nepheg and Zichri.
verses.6:22: And the sons of Uzziel: Elzaphan and Sithri.
verses.6:23: Now Aaron took Elisheba, the daughter of Amminadab, sister of Nahshon, to himself as a wife, and she bore to him Nadab and Abihu and Eleazar and Ithamar.
verses.6:24: And the sons of Korah: Assir and Elkanah and Abiasaph; these are the generations of Korah.
verses.6:25: And Eleazar, the son of Aaron, took one of the daughters of Putiel to himself as a wife, and she bore to him Phinehas; these are the heads of the paternal house of the Levites according to their generations.
verses.6:26: This is that Aaron and Moses to whom God said to bring out the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt with their host.
verses.6:27: These are the ones who spoke with Pharaoh king of Egypt; and they brought out the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt—the same Aaron and Moses.
verses.6:28: On the day when the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
verses.6:29: then the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, "I am the Lord; speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt, and I speak to you."
verses.6:30: And Moses said before the Lord, "Behold, I am faltering of speech, and how will Pharaoh listen to me?"
verses.7:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, "Behold, I have appointed you as a god to Pharaoh, and Aaron your brother shall be your prophet.
verses.7:2: You shall speak to him all the things that I command you, and Aaron your brother shall speak to Pharaoh, that he send away the sons of Israel out of his land.
verses.7:3: Yet I will harden the heart of Pharaoh, and I will multiply My signs and wonders in the land of Egypt.
verses.7:4: And Pharaoh will not listen to you; and I will lay My hand upon Egypt, and I will bring out My people, the sons of Israel, with My power out of the land of Egypt with great vengeance.
verses.7:5: And all the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord, when I stretch out My hand upon Egypt; and I will bring out the sons of Israel from their midst."
verses.7:6: So Moses and Aaron did just as the Lord commanded them; thus they did.
verses.7:7: Now Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron his brother was eighty-three years old, when he spoke to Pharaoh.
verses.7:8: And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
verses.7:9: "And if Pharaoh speaks to you, saying, 'Give us a sign or a wonder,' then you shall say to Aaron your brother, 'Take the rod and cast it upon the ground before Pharaoh and before his attendants, and it shall become a dragon.'"
verses.7:10: So Moses and Aaron went in before Pharaoh and his attendants, and they did thus, just as the Lord had commanded them; and Aaron cast down the rod before Pharaoh and before his attendants, and it became a dragon.
verses.7:11: Then Pharaoh summoned the wise men of Egypt and the sorcerers; and the enchanters of the Egyptians also did likewise with their sorceries,
verses.7:12: and each one cast down his rod, and they became dragons; yet the rod of Aaron swallowed up their rods.
verses.7:13: And the heart of Pharaoh grew hard, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had commanded them.
verses.7:14: And the Lord said to Moses, "The heart of Pharaoh is weighed down, so that he will not send away the people.
verses.7:15: Go to Pharaoh in the morning; behold, he is going out to the water, and you shall stand to meet him upon the bank of the river; and the rod that was turned into a serpent you shall take in your hand,
verses.7:16: and you shall say to him, 'The Lord God of the Hebrews has sent me to you, saying, "Send away My people, that they may serve Me in the wilderness"; and behold, you have not listened until now.
verses.7:17: Thus says the Lord, "By this you shall know that I am the Lord: behold, I strike with the rod that is in My hand upon the water that is in the river, and it shall turn into blood;
verses.7:18: and the fish that are in the river shall die, and the river shall grow foul, and the Egyptians shall not be able to drink water from the river."'"
verses.7:19: And the Lord said to Moses, "Say to Aaron your brother, 'Take your rod in your hand, and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt, and over their rivers, and over their canals, and over their marshes, and over all their standing water, and it shall become blood.'" And there was blood throughout all the land of Egypt, both in the wood and in the stone.
verses.7:20: And Moses and Aaron did thus, just as the Lord had commanded them; and lifting up his rod, he struck the water that was in the river before Pharaoh and before his attendants, and all the water that was in the river turned into blood.
verses.7:21: And the fish that were in the river died, and the river grew foul, and the Egyptians could not drink water from the river; and the blood was throughout all the land of Egypt.
verses.7:22: Yet the enchanters of the Egyptians also did likewise with their sorceries; and the heart of Pharaoh grew hard, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had said.
verses.7:23: Then Pharaoh turned and went into his house, and he did not set his mind even upon this.
verses.7:24: And all the Egyptians dug all around the river so as to drink water from the river, yet they could not drink water from the river.
verses.7:25: And seven days were fulfilled after the Lord struck the river.
verses.7:26: And the Lord said to Moses, "Go in to Pharaoh, and you shall say to him, 'Thus says the Lord, "Send away My people, that they may serve Me.
verses.7:27: Yet if you are not willing to send them away, behold, I strike all your borders with frogs.
verses.7:28: And the river shall pour forth frogs; and coming up they shall enter into your houses, and into the inner chambers of your bedrooms, and upon your beds, and into the houses of your attendants and of your people, and into your dough and into your ovens;
verses.7:29: and upon you, and upon your attendants, and upon your people the frogs shall come up."'"
verses.8:1: And the Lord said to Moses, "Say to Aaron your brother, 'Stretch out your staff with your hand over the rivers and over the canals and over the marshes, and bring up the frogs.'"
verses.8:2: And Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt and brought up the frogs; and the frog was brought up and covered the land of Egypt.
verses.8:3: Then the enchanters of the Egyptians also did likewise with their sorceries, and brought up the frogs upon the land of Egypt.
verses.8:4: And Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron and said, "Pray for me to the Lord, and let Him take away the frogs from me and from my people, and I will send them away, and they shall sacrifice to the Lord."
verses.8:5: And Moses said to Pharaoh, "Appoint for me when I should pray for you and for your servants and for your people, to destroy the frogs from you and from your people and from your houses; only in the river shall they remain."
verses.8:6: And he said, "For tomorrow." So he said, "As you have spoken, that you may see that there is no other besides the Lord;
verses.8:7: and the frogs shall be taken away from you and from your houses and from the courtyards and from your servants and from your people; only in the river shall they remain."
verses.8:8: Then Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh; and Moses cried out to the Lord concerning the appointed limit for the frogs, as Pharaoh had arranged.
verses.8:9: And the Lord did just as Moses had said, and the frogs died out of the houses and out of the courtyards and out of the fields.
verses.8:10: And they gathered them in heaps upon heaps, and the land stank.
verses.8:11: But when Pharaoh saw that there was relief, his heart became heavy, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had spoken.
verses.8:12: And the Lord said to Moses, "Say to Aaron, 'Stretch out your staff with your hand and strike the dust of the earth, and there shall be gnats both on men and on four-footed beasts and in all the land of Egypt.'"
verses.8:13: So Aaron stretched out the staff with his hand and struck the dust of the earth, and the gnats came upon men and upon four-footed beasts; and in all the dust of the earth there were gnats.
verses.8:14: Then the enchanters also did likewise with their sorceries to bring forth the gnat, and they could not; and the gnats were on men and on four-footed beasts.
verses.8:15: So the enchanters said to Pharaoh, "This is the finger of God." Yet the heart of Pharaoh was hardened, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had spoken.
verses.8:16: And the Lord said to Moses, "Rise early in the morning and stand before Pharaoh; and behold, he will come out to the water, and you shall say to him, 'Thus says the Lord: Send away My people, that they may serve Me in the wilderness;
verses.8:17: but if you are not willing to send away My people, behold, I am sending upon you and upon your servants and upon your people and upon your houses the dog-fly; and the houses of the Egyptians shall be filled with the dog-fly, and also the land upon which they are.
verses.8:18: And I will wonderfully distinguish in that day the land of Goshen, upon which My people are, where the dog-fly shall not be, that you may know that I am the Lord, the Lord of all the earth.
verses.8:19: And I will set a distinction between My people and your people; and tomorrow this shall be upon the land.'"
verses.8:20: And the Lord did so, and the dog-fly came in a multitude into the houses of Pharaoh and into the houses of his servants and into all the land of Egypt; and the land was ruined by the dog-fly.
verses.8:21: Then Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron, saying, "Go, sacrifice to your God in the land."
verses.8:22: And Moses said, "It is not possible for this matter to be done thus, for we shall sacrifice the abominations of the Egyptians to the Lord our God; for if we sacrifice the abominations of the Egyptians before them, we shall be stoned.
verses.8:23: We will go a journey of three days into the wilderness, and we will sacrifice to our God just as the Lord has said to us."
verses.8:24: And Pharaoh said, "I will send you away, and sacrifice to your God in the wilderness; only you shall not extend your journey far away. Pray therefore for me to the Lord."
verses.8:25: And Moses said, "Behold, I will go out from you and pray to God, and the dog-fly shall depart from you and from your servants and your people tomorrow; do not continue any longer, Pharaoh, to deceive, so as not to send away the people to sacrifice to the Lord."
verses.8:26: Then Moses went out from Pharaoh and prayed to God.
verses.8:27: And the Lord did just as Moses had said, and He took away the dog-fly from Pharaoh and from his servants and from his people, and not even one was left.
verses.8:28: And Pharaoh made his heart heavy at this time also, and he was not willing to send away the people.
verses.9:1: And the Lord said to Moses, "Go in to Pharaoh and say to him, 'Thus says the Lord, the God of the Hebrews: Send away My people, that they may serve Me;
verses.9:2: for if you are not willing to send away My people, but still hold fast to them,
verses.9:3: behold, the hand of the Lord shall be upon your livestock that are in the fields—upon the horses, and upon the beasts of burden, and the camels, and the oxen, and the sheep—a very great pestilence.
verses.9:4: And I will make a wonderful distinction at that time between the livestock of the Egyptians and the livestock of the sons of Israel; not a single thing shall die of all that belongs to the sons of Israel.'"
verses.9:5: And God set an appointed time, saying, "Tomorrow the Lord will do this thing in the land."
verses.9:6: And the Lord did this thing on the next day, and all the livestock of the Egyptians died; but of the livestock of the sons of Israel, not one died.
verses.9:7: But when Pharaoh saw that not one of all the livestock of the sons of Israel had died, the heart of Pharaoh became heavy, and he did not send away the people.
verses.9:8: And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying, "Take for yourselves handfuls of soot from a furnace, and let Moses scatter it toward heaven before Pharaoh and before his servants,
verses.9:9: and let it become dust over all the land of Egypt; and upon men and upon four-footed beasts there shall be boils, erupting blisters, both upon men and upon four-footed beasts and throughout all the land of Egypt."
verses.9:10: So he took the soot of the furnace before Pharaoh, and Moses scattered it toward heaven; and boils, erupting blisters, came upon men and upon four-footed beasts.
verses.9:11: And the sorcerers could not stand before Moses because of the boils; for the boils were upon the sorcerers and throughout all the land of Egypt.
verses.9:12: But the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had appointed.
verses.9:13: And the Lord said to Moses, "Rise early in the morning and stand before Pharaoh, and you shall say to him, 'Thus says the Lord, the God of the Hebrews: Send away My people, that they may serve Me.
verses.9:14: For at this present time I am sending forth all My afflictions into your heart and that of your servants and of your people, that you may know that there is no other like Me in all the earth.
verses.9:15: For now, stretching out My hand, I will strike you and put your people to death, and you shall be blotted out from the earth;
verses.9:16: and for this very reason you have been preserved, that I may display My strength in you, and that My name may be proclaimed in all the earth.
verses.9:17: Do you then still lay claim to My people, so as not to send them away?
verses.9:18: Behold, at this very hour tomorrow I will rain down exceedingly heavy hail, such as has never been in Egypt from the day it was founded until this day.
verses.9:19: Now therefore, hasten to gather your livestock and all that you have in the field; for all the men and the livestock that you have in the field, and that do not enter into a house, when the hail falls upon them, they shall die.'"
verses.9:20: He who feared the word of the Lord among the servants of Pharaoh gathered his livestock into the houses;
verses.9:21: but he who did not give heed in his mind to the word of the Lord left the livestock in the fields.
verses.9:22: And the Lord said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand toward heaven, and there shall be hail upon all the land of Egypt, both upon men and upon livestock and upon every plant that is upon the earth."
verses.9:23: And Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven, and the Lord sent thunderings and hail, and fire ran across the earth; and the Lord rained hail upon all the land of Egypt.
verses.9:24: So there was hail, and fire blazing within the hail; and the hail was exceedingly heavy, such as had never been in Egypt from the day a nation came into being upon it.
verses.9:25: And the hail struck throughout all the land of Egypt from man to livestock; and the hail struck every plant that was in the field, and the hail shattered all the trees that were in the fields.
verses.9:26: Only in the land of Goshen, where the sons of Israel were, there was no hail.
verses.9:27: Then Pharaoh sent and called Moses and Aaron, and said to them, "I have sinned this time; the Lord is righteous, and I and my people are ungodly.
verses.9:28: Pray therefore for me to the Lord, and let the thunderings of God and hail and fire cease to be; and I will send you away, and you shall no longer continue to remain."
verses.9:29: And Moses said to him, "As soon as I go out of the city, I will spread out my hands, and the thunderings shall cease, and the hail and the rain shall be no more, that you may know that the earth is the Lord's.
verses.9:30: Yet as for you and your servants, I know that you do not yet fear God."
verses.9:31: Now the flax and the barley were struck, for the barley was standing ripe, and the flax was in seed;
verses.9:32: but the wheat and the spelt were not struck, for they were late.
verses.9:33: So Moses went out from Pharaoh, outside the city, and stretched out his hands to the Lord; and the thunderings and the hail ceased, and the rain dropped no more upon the earth.
verses.9:34: And when Pharaoh saw that the rain and the hail and the thunderings had ceased, he continued to sin, and he made heavy his own heart and that of his servants.
verses.9:35: And the heart of Pharaoh was hardened, and he did not send away the sons of Israel, just as the Lord had spoken to Moses.
verses.10:1: Now the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, "Go in to Pharaoh; for I have hardened his heart and the hearts of his servants, that these signs may come upon them in succession,
verses.10:2: in order that you may recount in the ears of your children and to your children's children all the ways I have mocked the Egyptians, and My signs which I have performed among them; and you shall know that I am the Lord."
verses.10:3: So Moses and Aaron went in before Pharaoh and said to him, "Thus says the Lord God of the Hebrews: 'How long are you unwilling to revere Me? Send away My people, that they may serve Me.
verses.10:4: Yet if you are unwilling to send away My people, behold, tomorrow at this hour I will bring locusts in abundance upon all your borders;
verses.10:5: and they shall cover the face of the land, and you shall not be able to see the land; and they shall devour every remnant of the land that was left behind, which the hail left for you, and they shall devour every tree that grows for you upon the land;
verses.10:6: and your houses shall be filled, and the houses of your servants, and all the houses in all the land of the Egyptians—such things as neither your fathers nor their forefathers have ever seen, from the day they came to be upon the earth until this day.'" And Moses turned aside and went out from Pharaoh.
verses.10:7: Then the servants of Pharaoh said to him, "How long shall this be a stumbling block to us? Send the men away, so that they may serve their God. Or do you wish to know that Egypt has perished?"
verses.10:8: So they brought both Moses and Aaron back to Pharaoh, and he said to them, "Go and serve your God; but who and who are those who are going?"
verses.10:9: And Moses said, "With the young men and the elders we shall go, with our sons and daughters and sheep and cattle; for it is a feast of the Lord."
verses.10:10: And he said to them, "Let it be so, the Lord be with you; as I send you away, surely not your dependents also? See, for evil lies before you.
verses.10:11: Not so! Rather, let the men go and serve God, for this is what you yourselves were seeking." And they drove them out from the presence of Pharaoh.
verses.10:12: Then the Lord said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt, and let the locusts come up upon the land, and they shall devour every herb of the land and all the fruit of the trees which the hail left behind."
verses.10:13: And Moses lifted up the staff toward heaven, and he brought a south wind upon the land all that day and all the night; morning came, and the south wind took up the locusts,
verses.10:14: and brought them up over all the land of Egypt, and they settled upon all the borders of Egypt in exceeding multitude; before them there had never been such locusts, nor after them shall it be so again.
verses.10:15: And they covered the face of the land, and the land was ruined; and they devoured every herb of the land and all the fruit of the trees which had been left from the hail; nothing green was left on the trees or among any herb of the field in the land of Egypt.
verses.10:16: Then Pharaoh made haste to summon Moses and Aaron, saying, "I have sinned before the Lord your God and against you;
verses.10:17: therefore forgive my sin yet this once, and pray to the Lord your God, and let Him take away this death from me."
verses.10:18: So Moses went out from Pharaoh and prayed to God.
verses.10:19: And the Lord turned a mighty wind from the sea, and it took up the locusts and cast them into the Red Sea; and not one locust remained in all the land of Egypt.
verses.10:20: But the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh, and he did not send away the sons of Israel.
verses.10:21: Then the Lord said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand toward heaven, and let there be darkness over the land of Egypt, a darkness that can be felt."
verses.10:22: So Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven, and there came darkness, gloom, and tempest over all the land of Egypt for three days.
verses.10:23: And no one saw his brother for three days, and no one rose up from his bed for three days; but for all the sons of Israel there was light in all the places where they dwelt.
verses.10:24: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron, saying, "Go, serve the Lord your God; only leave behind the sheep and the cattle; and let your dependents depart with you."
verses.10:25: And Moses said, "Indeed, you yourself shall also give us burnt offerings and sacrifices, which we shall offer to the Lord our God,
verses.10:26: and our livestock shall go with us, and we shall not leave a single hoof behind; for from them we shall take to serve the Lord our God, and we do not know with what we shall serve the Lord our God until we come there."
verses.10:27: But the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh, and he was unwilling to send them away.
verses.10:28: And Pharaoh said, "Depart from me! Take heed to yourself lest you see my face again; for on whatever day you appear before me, you shall die."
verses.10:29: And Moses said, "You have spoken it; I shall no longer appear before your face."
verses.11:1: Now the Lord said to Moses, "Yet one more plague I will bring upon Pharaoh and upon Egypt, and after these things he will send you away from here; and when he sends you away, with everything he will utterly drive you out.
verses.11:2: Speak therefore secretly in the ears of the people, and let each one ask from his neighbor articles of silver and of gold, and clothing."
verses.11:3: And the Lord gave favor to His people in the sight of the Egyptians, and they lent to them; and the man Moses became exceedingly great in the sight of the Egyptians, and in the sight of Pharaoh, and in the sight of all his servants.
verses.11:4: And Moses said, "Thus says the Lord: 'About midnight I am going into the midst of Egypt;
verses.11:5: and every firstborn in the land of Egypt shall die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sits upon the throne, even to the firstborn of the maidservant who is beside the mill, and to the firstborn of every beast;
verses.11:6: and there shall be a great outcry throughout all the land of Egypt, the like of which has never been, and the like of which shall never be repeated.
verses.11:7: Yet among all the sons of Israel no dog shall growl with its tongue, not even from man to beast, that you may see how wondrously the Lord makes distinction between the Egyptians and Israel.'
verses.11:8: And all these servants of yours shall come down to me and bow down to me, saying, 'Go out, you and all your people whom you lead!' And after this I will go out." Then Moses went out from Pharaoh in wrath.
verses.11:9: And the Lord said to Moses, "Pharaoh will not heed you, so that I may exceedingly multiply My signs and My wonders in the land of Egypt."
verses.11:10: Now Moses and Aaron performed all these signs and wonders in the land of Egypt before Pharaoh; yet the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh, and he did not consent to send away the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt.
verses.12:1: Now the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,
verses.12:2: "This month shall be the beginning of months for you; it is the first for you among the months of the year.
verses.12:3: Speak to all the congregation of the sons of Israel, saying, 'On the tenth day of this month, let each one take a sheep according to the houses of their fathers, each one a sheep for a household.
verses.12:4: And if those in the household are too few so as not to be enough for a sheep, he shall take along with himself his neighbor who is nearest to him; according to the number of souls, each one shall reckon what is sufficient for himself toward a sheep.
verses.12:5: It shall be to you an unblemished sheep, a male a year old; you shall take it from the lambs and from the young goats.
verses.12:6: And it shall be kept by you until the fourteenth day of this month; and the entire multitude of the congregation of the sons of Israel shall slaughter it toward evening.
verses.12:7: And they shall take some of the blood and put it on the two doorposts and on the lintel in the houses in which they shall eat them.
verses.12:8: And they shall eat the flesh on this night, roasted with fire, and they shall eat unleavened bread with bitter herbs.
verses.12:9: You shall not eat any of them raw, nor boiled in water, but only roasted with fire—the head together with the feet and the inward parts.
verses.12:10: Nothing shall be left of it until morning, and a bone shall not be broken from it; but what remains of it until morning you shall burn thoroughly with fire.
verses.12:11: And thus you shall eat it: with your loins girded, your sandals on your feet, and your staffs in your hands; and you shall eat it in haste. It is a Passover to the Lord.
verses.12:12: And I will come into the land of Egypt on this night and will strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from man to beast; and upon all the gods of the Egyptians I will execute vengeance. I am the Lord.
verses.12:13: And the blood shall be for you as a sign upon the houses in which you are; and I will see the blood and will shelter you, and there shall not be among you a plague to destroy you when I strike in the land of Egypt.
verses.12:14: And this day shall be to you a memorial, and you shall celebrate it as a feast to the Lord throughout all your generations; you shall celebrate it as an everlasting ordinance.
verses.12:15: Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread; and from the first day you shall put away leaven out of your houses. Everyone who eats leaven, that soul shall be utterly destroyed from Israel, from the first day until the seventh day.
verses.12:16: And the first day shall be called holy, and the seventh day shall be a holy convocation to you; you shall do no servile work on them, except whatever shall be prepared for every soul—that alone shall be prepared for you.
verses.12:17: And you shall keep this commandment; for on this very day I will bring out your host from the land of Egypt. And you shall observe this day throughout your generations as an everlasting ordinance.
verses.12:18: Beginning on the fourteenth day of the first month, from evening you shall eat unleavened bread, until the twenty-first day of the month, until evening.
verses.12:19: For seven days no leaven shall be found in your houses; everyone who eats anything leavened, that soul shall be utterly destroyed from the congregation of Israel, both among the sojourners and the native-born of the land.
verses.12:20: You shall eat nothing leavened; in every dwelling place of yours you shall eat unleavened bread.'"
verses.12:21: Then Moses called the entire council of elders of the sons of Israel and said to them, "Go and take for yourselves a sheep according to your kindred, and sacrifice the Passover.
verses.12:22: And you shall take a bunch of hyssop, and dipping it in the blood that is beside the door, you shall touch the lintel and both doorposts with some of the blood that is beside the door; and none of you shall go out through the door of his house until morning.
verses.12:23: And the Lord will pass through to strike the Egyptians, and He will see the blood on the lintel and on both doorposts; and the Lord will pass over the door and will not permit the destroyer to enter your houses to strike.
verses.12:24: And you shall keep this word as an ordinance for yourself and for your sons forever.
verses.12:25: And when you enter the land which the Lord shall give you, just as He spoke, you shall keep this service.
verses.12:26: And it shall come to pass, when your sons say to you, 'What is this service?'
verses.12:27: then you shall say to them, 'This Passover is a sacrifice to the Lord, because He sheltered the houses of the sons of Israel in Egypt when He struck the Egyptians and delivered our houses.'" And the people bowed down and worshiped.
verses.12:28: And the sons of Israel went and did just as the Lord had commanded Moses; so they did.
verses.12:29: Now it came to pass at midnight that the Lord struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sat on the throne to the firstborn of the captive woman who was in the dungeon, and even to the firstborn of every beast.
verses.12:30: And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he and his servants and all the Egyptians; and there arose a great outcry in all the land of Egypt, for there was not a house in which there was not someone dead.
verses.12:31: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron by night and said to them, "Rise up and go out from among my people, both you and the sons of Israel; go and serve the Lord your God, just as you say.
verses.12:32: Take along both your sheep and your oxen and depart, and bless me also."
verses.12:33: And the Egyptians pressed the people hard to drive them out of the land in haste, for they said, "We are all dying."
verses.12:34: So the people took up their dough before it was leavened, with their batches of dough bound up in their garments upon their shoulders.
verses.12:35: And the sons of Israel did just as Moses had instructed them, and they asked from the Egyptians articles of silver and gold, and clothing.
verses.12:36: And the Lord gave favor to His people in the sight of the Egyptians, and they lent to them; thus they plundered the Egyptians.
verses.12:37: Then the sons of Israel set out from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand men on foot, besides the dependents.
verses.12:38: And a great mixed multitude went up with them, along with sheep and oxen and exceedingly many livestock.
verses.12:39: And they baked the dough which they had brought out of Egypt into unleavened hearth-cakes, for it was not leavened; because the Egyptians had driven them out and they could not delay, nor had they prepared provisions for themselves for the journey.
verses.12:40: Now the dwelling of the sons of Israel, which they dwelt in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan, was four hundred and thirty-five years.
verses.12:41: And it came to pass after the four hundred and thirty-five years that the entire host of the Lord went out from the land of Egypt by night.
verses.12:42: It is a vigil to the Lord for bringing them out of the land of Egypt; that very night is a vigil to the Lord, to be for all the sons of Israel throughout their generations.
verses.12:43: And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying, "This is the law of the Passover: no foreigner shall eat of it;
verses.12:44: and every household servant or one bought with silver, you shall circumcise him, and then he shall eat of it.
verses.12:45: A temporary resident or a hired servant shall not eat of it.
verses.12:46: In one house it shall be eaten; you shall not carry any of the flesh outside the house, and you shall not break a bone of it.
verses.12:47: All the congregation of the sons of Israel shall keep it.
verses.12:48: And if any proselyte comes to you to keep the Passover to the Lord, you shall circumcise every male belonging to him, and then he shall draw near to keep it, and he shall be just like the native-born of the land; no uncircumcised person shall eat of it.
verses.12:49: There shall be one law for the native and for the proselyte who has come among you."
verses.12:50: And the sons of Israel did just as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron concerning them; so they did.
verses.12:51: And it came to pass on that day that the Lord brought the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt with their host.
verses.13:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.13:2: "Sanctify to Me every firstborn, first-produced, opening every womb among the sons of Israel, from man even to beast; it is Mine."
verses.13:3: And Moses said to the people, "Remember this day in which you came out from the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage; for with a mighty hand the Lord brought you out from here, and leaven shall not be eaten.
verses.13:4: For on this day you are going out, in the month of the new crops.
verses.13:5: And it shall be, when the Lord your God brings you into the land of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Hivites, and the Girgashites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Jebusites, which He swore to your fathers to give you, a land flowing with milk and honey, that you shall perform this service in this month.
verses.13:6: Six days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day is a feast of the Lord.
verses.13:7: Unleavened bread you shall eat seven days; nothing leavened shall be seen with you, nor shall there be leaven with you in all your borders.
verses.13:8: And you shall declare to your son in that day, saying, 'Because of this the Lord God did for me when I was coming out of Egypt.'
verses.13:9: And it shall be to you a sign upon your hand and a memorial before your eyes, so that the law of the Lord may be in your mouth; for with a mighty hand the Lord God brought you out of Egypt.
verses.13:10: And you shall keep this law from days to days.
verses.13:11: And it shall be, when the Lord your God brings you into the land of the Canaanites, in the manner He swore to your fathers, and gives it to you,
verses.13:12: that you shall set apart every opener of the womb, the males, to the Lord; every opener of the womb from the herds or among your beasts, as many as shall be born to you, the males you shall sanctify to the Lord.
verses.13:13: Every opener of the womb of a donkey you shall exchange with a sheep; and if you do not exchange it, you shall redeem it. Every firstborn of man among your sons you shall redeem.
verses.13:14: And if your son asks you hereafter, saying, 'What is this?' then you shall say to him, 'With a mighty hand the Lord brought us out from the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage;
verses.13:15: and when Pharaoh hardened himself against sending us away, He slew every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of men even to the firstborn of beasts; therefore I sacrifice every firstborn to the Lord, every opener of the womb, the males, and every firstborn of my sons I will redeem.'
verses.13:16: And it shall be for a sign upon your hand, and an immovable token before your eyes; for with a mighty hand the Lord brought you out of Egypt."
verses.13:17: Now when Pharaoh sent the people away, God did not lead them by the way of the land of the Philistines, because it was near; for God said, "Lest at any time the people change their mind upon seeing war, and return to Egypt."
verses.13:18: And God led the people around by the way into the wilderness, to the Red Sea; and in the fifth generation the sons of Israel went up out of the land of Egypt.
verses.13:19: And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him; for he had bound the sons of Israel by an oath, saying, "The Lord will surely visit you, and you shall carry up my bones from here with you."
verses.13:20: And setting out from Succoth, the sons of Israel encamped at Etham, beside the wilderness.
verses.13:21: And God went before them, by day in a pillar of cloud to show them the way, and by night in a pillar of fire.
verses.13:22: And the pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night did not fail before all the people.
verses.14:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.14:2: "Speak to the sons of Israel, that they turn back and encamp opposite the farmstead, between Migdol and the sea, over against Baal Zephon; before them you shall encamp by the sea,
verses.14:3: and Pharaoh will say to his people, 'These sons of Israel are wandering in the land; for the wilderness has shut them in.'
verses.14:4: And I will harden the heart of Pharaoh, and he shall pursue after them; and I shall be glorified in Pharaoh and in all his army, and all the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord." And they did so.
verses.14:5: And it was reported to the king of the Egyptians that the people had fled; and the heart of Pharaoh and the heart of his servants turned against the people, and they said, "What is this we have done, to send away the sons of Israel from serving us?"
verses.14:6: Therefore Pharaoh harnessed his chariots, and took all his people along with him,
verses.14:7: taking six hundred chosen chariots, and all the cavalry of the Egyptians, and officers over all of them.
verses.14:8: And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt and of his servants, and he pursued after the sons of Israel; and the sons of Israel were going out with a high hand.
verses.14:9: And the Egyptians pursued after them, and found them encamped by the sea, all the cavalry and the chariots of Pharaoh, and his horsemen and his army, opposite the farmstead, over against Baal Zephon.
verses.14:10: And Pharaoh drew near; and the sons of Israel lifted up their eyes and saw, and the Egyptians had encamped behind them, and they were exceedingly afraid. And the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord;
verses.14:11: and they said to Moses, "Because there were no graves in the land of Egypt, have you brought us out to put us to death in the wilderness? What is this you have done to us, bringing us out of Egypt?
verses.14:12: Was this not the word that we spoke to you in Egypt, saying, 'Leave us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians'? For it is better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in this wilderness."
verses.14:13: And Moses said to the people, "Take courage! Stand firm and see the salvation from God, which He will work for us today; for in the manner that you have seen the Egyptians today, you shall never again see them forevermore.
verses.14:14: The Lord shall fight for you, and you shall be silent."
verses.14:15: And the Lord said to Moses, "Why do you cry out to Me? Speak to the sons of Israel, and let them break camp;
verses.14:16: and you, lift up your rod, and stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it, and let the sons of Israel go into the midst of the sea on dry ground.
verses.14:17: And behold, I will harden the heart of Pharaoh and of all the Egyptians, and they shall go in after them; and I shall be glorified in Pharaoh and in all his army, and in his chariots and in his horses.
verses.14:18: And all the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord, when I am glorified in Pharaoh and in his chariots and horses."
verses.14:19: And the angel of God, who went before the camp of the sons of Israel, moved and went behind them; and the pillar of cloud also moved from before them and stood behind them.
verses.14:20: And it entered between the Egyptians and the camp of Israel, and stood; and there came darkness and gloom, and the night passed, and they did not mingle with one another all the night.
verses.14:21: And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and the Lord drove back the sea with a strong south wind all the night, and made the sea dry land, and the water was divided.
verses.14:22: And the sons of Israel went into the midst of the sea on the dry ground, and the water was to them a wall on the right hand and a wall on the left.
verses.14:23: And the Egyptians pursued, and went in after them, even every horse of Pharaoh, and the chariots, and the riders, into the midst of the sea.
verses.14:24: And it came to pass in the morning watch that the Lord looked down upon the camp of the Egyptians in the pillar of fire and cloud, and threw the camp of the Egyptians into confusion,
verses.14:25: and bound fast the axles of their chariots, and drove them with difficulty. And the Egyptians said, "Let us flee from the face of Israel, for the Lord is fighting for them against the Egyptians."
verses.14:26: And the Lord said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand over the sea, that the water may be restored and cover over the Egyptians, both upon the chariots and the riders."
verses.14:27: And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the water was restored toward daybreak to its place; and the Egyptians fled beneath the water, and the Lord shook off the Egyptians in the midst of the sea.
verses.14:28: And the returning water covered the chariots and the riders and all the host of Pharaoh that had gone in after them into the sea; and not even one of them was left.
verses.14:29: But the sons of Israel walked through dry land in the midst of the sea, and the water was to them a wall on the right hand and a wall on the left.
verses.14:30: And the Lord delivered Israel in that day from the hand of the Egyptians; and Israel saw the Egyptians dead upon the shore of the sea.
verses.14:31: And Israel saw the mighty hand, the things which the Lord had done to the Egyptians; and the people feared the Lord, and believed in God and in Moses His servant.
verses.15:1: Then Moses and the sons of Israel sang this song to God, speaking these words: "Let us sing to the Lord, for gloriously has He been glorified; both horse and rider He has cast into the sea.
verses.15:2: A helper and a defender has He become to me for deliverance; this is my God, and I shall glorify Him—the God of my father, and I shall exalt Him.
verses.15:3: The Lord is the One who shatters wars; the Lord is His name.
verses.15:4: The chariots of Pharaoh and his armed force He has cast into the sea, along with chosen officers who rode upon them; they were swallowed up in the Red Sea.
verses.15:5: With the open deep He covered them over; they sank downward into the abyss like a stone.
verses.15:6: Your right hand, O Lord, has been magnified in might; Your right hand, O Lord, has shattered foes.
verses.15:7: And in the abundance of Your glory You crushed the adversaries; You dispatched Your wrath, and it devoured them like dry stubble.
verses.15:8: And by the blast of Your indignation the water parted; the waters congealed like a wall, and the billows hardened in the midst of the sea.
verses.15:9: The foe declared, 'Pursuing them, I will overtake them; I will divide the plunder, I will satisfy my soul, I will slay with my sword, and my hand shall exercise dominion.'
verses.15:10: You sent forth Your breath, and the sea covered them; they plunged like lead into the surging water.
verses.15:11: Who is like You among the gods, O Lord? Who is like You? Glorified among the holy ones, wondrous in splendors, performing marvels.
verses.15:12: You stretched out Your right hand; the earth swallowed them down.
verses.15:13: In Your righteousness You guided this people of Yours whom You redeemed; by Your strength You summoned them onward to Your holy lodging place.
verses.15:14: Nations heard and grew furious; birth pangs seized the inhabitants of Philistia.
verses.15:15: Then the chieftains of Edom hastened in alarm; and as for the rulers of the Moabites, trembling gripped them; all the inhabitants of Canaan melted away.
verses.15:16: May terror and dread fall upon them; by the greatness of Your arm let them be turned to stone, until Your people pass through, O Lord, until this people of Yours whom You acquired pass through.
verses.15:17: Bring them in and plant them firmly upon the mountain of Your inheritance, in Your prepared habitation which You fashioned, O Lord—the sanctuary, O Lord, which Your hands made ready.
verses.15:18: The Lord is King forever, and to the age and even beyond!"
verses.15:19: For Pharaoh's cavalry entered the sea together with his chariots and horsemen, and the Lord brought the water of the sea back upon them; yet the sons of Israel journeyed across dry ground in the midst of the sea.
verses.15:20: Then Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took the timbrel in her hand, and all the women went forth behind her with timbrels and dancing.
verses.15:21: And Miriam led them in song, declaring, "Let us sing to the Lord, for gloriously has He been glorified; both horse and rider He has cast into the sea."
verses.15:22: Now Moses led the sons of Israel away from the Red Sea and brought them into the wilderness of Shur; and they traveled three days in the wilderness without finding water to drink.
verses.15:23: Then they arrived at Marah, yet they were unable to drink from Marah, for it was bitter; on account of this he named that place Bitterness.
verses.15:24: And the people murmured against Moses, saying, "What are we to drink?"
verses.15:25: So Moses cried aloud to the Lord, and the Lord showed him a piece of wood, and he threw it into the water, and the water grew sweet. There He established for him ordinances and judgments, and there He put him to the test,
verses.15:26: and He said, "If you truly listen to the voice of the Lord your God, and perform what is pleasing in His sight, and give ear to His commandments, and keep all His ordinances, I will not bring upon you any of the diseases that I brought upon the Egyptians; for I am the Lord your God who heals you."
verses.15:27: Then they came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy trunks of palm trees; and they encamped there beside the waters.
verses.16:1: Then they departed from Elim, and the whole assembly of the sons of Israel came into the wilderness of Sin, which lies between Elim and Sinai. On the fifteenth day of the second month after they had come out of the land of Egypt,
verses.16:2: the entire assembly of the sons of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron;
verses.16:3: and the sons of Israel spoke to them, "If only we had died struck down by the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat beside the cauldrons of meat and ate loaves of bread to our fill! For you have led us out into this wilderness to put this whole assembly to death by famine."
verses.16:4: Then the Lord said to Moses, "Behold, I am raining down loaves of bread for you from heaven; and the people shall go out and gather each day's portion for that day, so that I may test them whether they will walk in My law or not.
verses.16:5: And it shall come to pass on the sixth day that they shall prepare whatever they bring in, and it shall be twice as much as what they gather day by day."
verses.16:6: So Moses and Aaron said to the whole assembly of the sons of Israel, "At evening you shall know that the Lord brought you out of the land of Egypt,
verses.16:7: and in the morning you shall behold the glory of the Lord, because He has heard your murmuring against God; for what are we, that you murmur against us?"
verses.16:8: Moses also said, "This shall be when the Lord gives you meat to eat at evening and loaves of bread in the morning to your fill, because the Lord has heard your murmuring with which you murmur against us; for what are we? Indeed, your murmuring is not against us, but rather against God."
verses.16:9: Then Moses said to Aaron, "Say to the whole assembly of the sons of Israel, 'Draw near before God, for He has heard your murmuring.'"
verses.16:10: Now while Aaron was speaking to the entire assembly of the sons of Israel, they turned toward the wilderness, and the glory of the Lord appeared in a cloud.
verses.16:11: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.16:12: "I have heard the murmuring of the sons of Israel; speak to them and say, 'Toward evening you shall eat meat, and in the morning you shall be filled with bread; and you shall know that I am the Lord your God.'"
verses.16:13: So evening came, and quail came up and covered the encampment; and in the morning it came about, as the dew settled all around the encampment,
verses.16:14: behold, upon the surface of the wilderness there lay something fine like coriander, white like frost upon the earth.
verses.16:15: When the sons of Israel saw it, they asked one another, "What is this?" For they did not know what it was. And Moses said to them, "This is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat.
verses.16:16: This is the word that the Lord has commanded: 'Gather from it, each person for those belonging to him; an omer per head, according to the number of your souls, each of you along with your tentmates shall collect.'"
verses.16:17: And the sons of Israel did so, and they gathered, one a large amount and another a smaller amount.
verses.16:18: Yet when they measured it by the omer, the one with much had no surplus, and the one with little suffered no lack; each had gathered for those belonging to his own household.
verses.16:19: Then Moses instructed them, "Let no one leave any of it behind until the morning."
verses.16:20: Yet they did not heed Moses, for certain ones left some of it behind until the morning; and it teemed with worms and gave off a stench. And Moses grew bitter against them.
verses.16:21: So they gathered it in the morning; and whenever the sun grew hot, it melted away.
verses.16:22: Now it happened on the sixth day that they gathered twice the needed portion, two omers for each person; and all the rulers of the assembly came in and reported it to Moses.
verses.16:23: And the Lord said to them, "Is this not the word that the Lord spoke? Tomorrow is a Sabbath, a holy rest to the Lord; whatever you would bake, bake, and whatever you would boil, boil; and all that remains over, set it aside for storage until the morning."
verses.16:24: So they set some of it aside until the morning, just as Moses had commanded them; and it did not give off a stench, nor was there any worm found in it.
verses.16:25: Then Moses said, "Eat it today, for today is a Sabbath to the Lord; it will not be found in the plain.
verses.16:26: Six days you shall gather, yet on the seventh day is a Sabbath, because there shall be none on it."
verses.16:27: Yet it came about on the seventh day that some of the people went out to gather, and they found nothing.
verses.16:28: Then the Lord said to Moses, "How long will you refuse to heed My commandments and My law?
verses.16:29: Behold, for the Lord has given you this day; on this account He Himself gave you bread for two days on the sixth day. Remain seated, each one in your own houses; let no one go forth from his place on the seventh day."
verses.16:30: So the people kept the Sabbath rest on the seventh day.
verses.16:31: And the sons of Israel called its name manna; now it was white like coriander seed, and its taste was like a wafer made with honey.
verses.16:32: Then Moses said, "This is the word that the Lord has commanded: 'Fill an omer with the manna for safekeeping throughout your generations, so that they may see the bread that you ate in the wilderness when the Lord led you out of the land of Egypt.'"
verses.16:33: And Moses said to Aaron, "Take one golden jar, and place into it a full omer of manna, and you shall lay it up before God for preservation throughout your generations,"
verses.16:34: in the manner that the Lord had commanded Moses; and Aaron laid it up before God for preservation.
verses.16:35: Now the sons of Israel ate the manna for forty years, until they entered the inhabited land; they ate the manna until they reached a region of Phoenicia.
verses.16:36: Now the omer was the tenth part of the three measures.
verses.17:1: And all the congregation of the sons of Israel departed from the wilderness of Sin, according to their encampments, by the word of the Lord, and encamped in Rephidim; yet there was no water for the people to drink.
verses.17:2: And the people reviled Moses, saying, "Give us water, that we may drink." And Moses said to them, "Why do you revile me, and why do you test the Lord?"
verses.17:3: And the people thirsted there for water, and the people murmured there against Moses, saying, "Why is this that you have brought us up out of Egypt, to slay us and our children and the livestock with thirst?"
verses.17:4: Then Moses cried out to the Lord, saying, "What shall I do with this people? Yet a little while, and they will stone me!"
verses.17:5: And the Lord said to Moses, "Go on before this people, and take with yourself some of the elders of the people; and take in your hand the rod with which you struck the river, and you shall go.
verses.17:6: Behold, I stand there before you upon the rock in Horeb; and you shall strike the rock, and water shall come forth out of it, and My people shall drink." And Moses did so in the sight of the sons of Israel.
verses.17:7: And he named the name of that place Testing and Reviling, because of the reviling of the sons of Israel, and because they tested the Lord, saying, "Is the Lord among us or not?"
verses.17:8: Now Amalek came and fought against Israel in Rephidim.
verses.17:9: And Moses said to Joshua, "Choose for yourself mighty men, and go out and array yourself in battle against Amalek tomorrow; and behold, I will stand upon the top of the hill, with the rod of God in my hand."
verses.17:10: And Joshua did just as Moses had told him, and went out and arrayed himself in battle against Amalek; and Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
verses.17:11: And it came to pass, whenever Moses lifted up his hands, that Israel prevailed; and whenever he let down his hands, Amalek prevailed.
verses.17:12: Now the hands of Moses were heavy; so they took a stone and placed it under him, and he sat upon it. And Aaron and Hur supported his hands, one on this side and one on that side; and the hands of Moses were held steady until the setting of the sun.
verses.17:13: And Joshua routed Amalek and all his people with the slaughter of the sword.
verses.17:14: Then the Lord said to Moses, "Write this down for a memorial in a book, and deliver it into the ears of Joshua, that I will utterly blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven."
verses.17:15: And Moses built an altar to the Lord, and named its name The Lord Is My Refuge;
verses.17:16: for with a hidden hand the Lord wages war against Amalek from generations to generations.
verses.18:1: Now Jethro, the priest of Midian, the father-in-law of Moses, heard all that the Lord had done for Israel His own people, for the Lord had brought Israel out of Egypt.
verses.18:2: And Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, took Zipporah, the wife of Moses, after her dismissal,
verses.18:3: and her two sons, the name of one of them being Gershom, saying, "I was a sojourner in a foreign land";
verses.18:4: and the name of the second was Eliezer, saying, "For the God of my father is my helper, and He delivered me out of the hand of Pharaoh."
verses.18:5: And Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, and the sons and the wife came out to Moses into the wilderness, where he encamped at the mountain of God.
verses.18:6: And it was reported to Moses, saying, "Behold, your father-in-law Jethro is coming to you, and your wife and your two sons with him."
verses.18:7: So Moses went out to meet his father-in-law, and bowed down before him and kissed him; and they greeted one another, and he brought him into the tent.
verses.18:8: And Moses recounted to his father-in-law all that the Lord had done to Pharaoh and to all the Egyptians for the sake of Israel, and all the hardship that had come upon them along the way, and how the Lord had delivered them out of the hand of Pharaoh and out of the hand of the Egyptians.
verses.18:9: And Jethro was amazed at all the good things which the Lord had done for them, in that He had delivered them out of the hand of the Egyptians and out of the hand of Pharaoh.
verses.18:10: And Jethro said, "Blessed be the Lord, because He has delivered them out of the hand of the Egyptians and out of the hand of Pharaoh.
verses.18:11: Now I know that the Lord is great above all the gods, on account of this, that they set upon them."
verses.18:12: And Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, took whole burnt offerings and sacrifices for God; and Aaron and all the elders of Israel came to eat bread together with the father-in-law of Moses before God.
verses.18:13: And it came to pass after the next day that Moses sat down to judge the people; and all the people stood before Moses from morning until evening.
verses.18:14: And when Jethro saw all that he was doing for the people, he said, "What is this that you are doing for the people? Why do you sit alone, while all the people stand before you from morning until evening?"
verses.18:15: And Moses said to his father-in-law, "Because the people come to me to seek judgment from God.
verses.18:16: For whenever a dispute arises among them and they come to me, I judge each one, and I instruct them in the ordinances of God and His law."
verses.18:17: And the father-in-law of Moses said to him, "You are not doing this thing rightly;
verses.18:18: you will surely waste away with unendurable exhaustion, both you and all the people who are with you; this matter is too heavy for you, and you will not be able to perform it alone.
verses.18:19: Now therefore listen to me, and I will give you counsel, and God shall be with you. Stand for the people in the things pertaining to God, and you shall bring their matters before God;
verses.18:20: and you shall solemnly testify to them the ordinances of God and His law, and you shall show them the ways in which they shall walk, and the works which they shall do.
