verses.35:19: and the holy garments of Aaron the priest, and the garments in which they shall minister, and the tunics of the priesthood for the sons of Aaron, and the anointing oil, and the compounded incense.'"
verses.35:20: And the entire congregation of the sons of Israel departed from Moses.
verses.35:21: And each one whose heart moved him, and as many as it pleased in their soul, brought up an offering; and they brought an offering to the Lord for all the works of the tabernacle of the testimony, and for all its workmanship, and for all the garments of the sanctuary.
verses.35:22: And the men brought from the women—everyone to whose mind it seemed good brought signets, and earrings, and rings, and hair ornaments, and armlets, every article of gold;
verses.35:23: even all those who brought offerings of gold to the Lord. And everyone with whom was found fine linen, and blue-dyed skins, and ram skins dyed red, brought them.
verses.35:24: And everyone who set apart an offering brought silver and bronze, the offerings to the Lord; and those with whom incorruptible wood was found brought it also for all the works of the construction.
verses.35:25: And every woman wise in mind to spin with her hands brought spun yarn: the blue, and the purple, and the scarlet, and the fine linen.
verses.35:26: And all the women to whose mind it seemed good in wisdom spun the goat hair.
verses.35:27: And the rulers brought the emerald stones and the stones for setting for the ephod and the oracle,
verses.35:28: and the spice mixtures, and the oil of anointing, and the composition of the incense.
verses.35:29: And every man and woman whose mind moved them to come in to do all the works that the Lord had commanded to be done through Moses—the sons of Israel brought an offering to the Lord.
verses.35:30: And Moses said to the sons of Israel, "Behold, God has called by name Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah,
verses.35:31: and has filled him with a spirit of wisdom and understanding and knowledge of all things,
verses.35:32: to act as master craftsman in all the works of craftsmanship, to work the gold and the silver and the bronze,
verses.35:33: and to carve the stone, and to work the wood, and to labor in every work of wisdom;
verses.35:34: and He has also put it in his mind to instruct, both him and Eliab the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan;
verses.35:35: He has filled them with wisdom and understanding of mind, to understand how to do all the works of the sanctuary, and to weave the woven and embroidered works with the scarlet and the fine linen, to perform every work of artistic craftsmanship."
verses.36:1: And Bezalel and Eliab worked, and every man wise in mind to whom wisdom and knowledge were given within them to understand how to perform all the works according to the sacred duties, according to all that the Lord commanded.
verses.36:2: And Moses called Bezalel and Eliab, and all those who possessed wisdom, to whom God had given knowledge in the heart, and all those willingly desiring to come forward to the works so as to complete them.
verses.36:3: And they received from Moses all the contributions which the sons of Israel had brought for all the works of the sanctuary to make them; and they continued to receive the offerings from those who brought them in the morning.
verses.36:4: And all the wise men who were performing the works of the sanctuary came, each according to his own work which they were doing.
verses.36:5: And he said to Moses, "The people are bringing an abundance for the works which the Lord commanded to do."
verses.36:6: And Moses gave a command, and proclaimed in the camp, saying, "Let neither man nor woman work any longer for the firstfruits of the sanctuary." And the people were restrained from bringing any more.
verses.36:7: And the works were sufficient for them to accomplish the construction, and they had some left over.
verses.36:8: And every wise man among those who did the work made the garments of the sanctuary, which are for Aaron the priest, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
verses.36:9: And he made the ephod of gold, and blue, and purple, and spun scarlet, and fine twisted linen.
verses.36:10: And the plates of gold were cut into hair-fine threads, so as to weave them together with the blue, and the purple, and the finely spun scarlet, and with the fine twisted linen; they made it as woven work,
verses.36:11: shoulder-pieces joining it together on both sides, woven work, intertwined with one another as one piece.
verses.36:12: Of the same piece they made it, of gold, and blue, and purple, and finely spun scarlet, and fine twisted linen, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
verses.36:13: And they made both stones of emerald, fastened in clasps and bordered with settings, and engraved with the engraving of a signet according to the names of the sons of Israel;
verses.36:14: and he placed them upon the shoulders of the ephod, as stones of remembrance for the sons of Israel, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
verses.36:15: And they made an oracle, woven work of embroidery, like the workmanship of the ephod, of gold, and blue, and purple, and finely spun scarlet, and fine twisted linen;
verses.36:16: they made the oracle foursquare and doubled, a span in length and a span in width, doubled.
verses.36:17: And a woven setting of stones in four rows was woven into it, a row of stones: a sardius, a topaz, and an emerald were the first row;
verses.36:18: and the second row: a carbuncle, a sapphire, and a jasper;
verses.36:19: and the third row: a ligure, an agate, and an amethyst;
verses.36:20: and the fourth row: a chrysolite, a beryl, and an onyx, encircled with gold and bound together with gold.
verses.36:21: And the stones were twelve, according to the names of the sons of Israel, engraved like signets according to their names, each one according to his own name, for the twelve tribes.
verses.36:22: And they made upon the oracle intertwined fringes, braided work, of pure gold.
verses.36:23: And they made two small shields of gold and two golden rings, and they placed the two golden rings upon both ends of the oracle;
verses.36:24: and they placed the braided cords of gold upon the rings on both sides of the oracle, and the two braided cords into the ends,
verses.36:25: and they placed them upon the two small shields; and they placed them upon the shoulders of the ephod opposite each other on the front.
verses.36:26: And they made two golden rings, and placed them upon the two corners at the edge of the oracle, and upon the edge of the back of the ephod on the inside.
verses.36:27: And they made two golden rings, and placed them upon both shoulders of the ephod.
verses.36:28: And he fastened the oracle tightly from the rings that were upon it to the rings of the ephod, held together by the blue, interwoven into the woven fabric of the ephod, so that the oracle might not become loose from the ephod, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
verses.36:29: And they made the robe beneath the ephod, woven work, wholly of blue;
verses.36:30: and the opening of the robe in the middle was woven through and braided together, having a border all around the opening so that it would not come apart.
verses.36:31: And they made upon the hem of the robe below little pomegranates, like a blossoming pomegranate, of blue, and purple, and spun scarlet, and fine twisted linen.
verses.36:32: And they made golden bells, and placed the bells upon the hem of the robe all around between the little pomegranates:
verses.36:33: a golden bell and a little pomegranate upon the hem of the robe all around, for ministering, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
verses.36:34: And they made tunics of fine linen, woven work, for Aaron and for his sons,
verses.36:35: and the turbans of fine linen, and the miter of fine linen, and the trousers of fine twisted linen,
verses.36:36: and their sashes of fine linen, and blue, and purple, and spun scarlet, the work of an embroiderer, in the manner that the Lord commanded Moses.
verses.36:37: And they made the golden plate, the consecration of the sanctuary, of pure gold; and he inscribed upon it letters carved like a signet: "Holiness to the Lord";
verses.36:38: and they placed it upon the blue border, so that it rested upon the miter above, in the manner that the Lord commanded Moses.
verses.37:1: And they made ten curtains for the tabernacle;
verses.37:2: the length of one curtain was twenty-eight cubits—they were all the same—and the width of one curtain was four cubits.
verses.37:3: And he made the veil of blue, and purple, and spun scarlet, and fine twisted linen, the work of a weaver, with cherubim;
verses.37:4: and they placed it upon four incorruptible pillars overlaid with gold; and their capitals were of gold, and their four bases were of silver.
verses.37:5: And they made the veil of the door of the tabernacle of the testimony of blue, and purple, and spun scarlet, and fine twisted linen, woven work of cherubim,
verses.37:6: and their five pillars and the rings; and they overlaid their capitals with gold, and the five bases were of bronze.
verses.37:7: And they made the court: on the side toward the southwest, hangings of the court of fine twisted linen, one hundred by one hundred;
verses.37:8: and their pillars were twenty, and their bases were twenty.
verses.37:9: And the side toward the north was one hundred by one hundred, and the side toward the south was one hundred by one hundred; and their pillars were twenty, and their bases were twenty.
verses.37:10: And on the side toward the sea were curtains of fifty cubits; their pillars were ten, and their bases were ten.
verses.37:11: And the side toward the east was fifty cubits, the part along the flank;
verses.37:12: and their pillars were three, and their bases were three.
verses.37:13: And upon the second flank, on this side and on that side by the gate of the court, were curtains of one hundred and fifty cubits; their pillars were three, and their bases were three.
verses.37:14: All the curtains of the tabernacle were of fine twisted linen;
verses.37:15: and the bases of their pillars were of bronze, and their hooks were of silver, and their capitals were overlaid with silver, and the pillars were overlaid with silver, all the pillars of the court.
verses.37:16: And the veil of the gate of the court was the work of an embroiderer, of blue, and purple, and spun scarlet, and fine twisted linen; twenty cubits was the length, and the height and the width were five cubits, matching the hangings of the court;
verses.37:17: and their pillars were four, and their four bases were of bronze, and their hooks were of silver, and their capitals were overlaid with silver.
verses.37:18: And they themselves were overlaid with silver, and all the pegs of the court all around were of bronze.
verses.37:19: And this is the arrangement of the tabernacle of the testimony, just as it was commanded to Moses, that the ministry should be that of the Levites through Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest.
verses.37:20: And Bezalel, the son of Uri, of the tribe of Judah, did just as the Lord commanded Moses,
verses.37:21: and Eliab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, who was the master craftsman of the woven works, and the needlework, and the embroidered works, to weave with the scarlet and with the fine linen.
verses.38:2: and overlaid it with pure gold inside and outside.
verses.38:3: And he cast four golden rings for it, two on the one side and two on the second side,
verses.38:4: wide for the poles, so as to carry it with them.
verses.38:5: And he made the mercy seat of gold above the ark,
verses.38:7: one cherub at the end of the mercy seat and one cherub at the second end of the mercy seat,
verses.38:8: overshadowing the mercy seat with their wings.
verses.38:9: And he made the table set forth of pure gold,
verses.38:10: and cast four rings for it, two on the one side and two on the second side, wide so as to carry it with the poles in them.
verses.38:11: And he made the poles of the ark and of the table, and overlaid them with gold.
verses.38:12: And he made the vessels of the table, the dishes, and the censers, and the cups, and the libation bowls with which he shall pour out drink offerings, of gold.
verses.38:13: And he made the lampstand that gives light of gold,
verses.38:14: solid in its shaft, and the branches from both of its sides;
verses.38:15: from its branches the buds extending out, three from the one side and three from the other, equal to one another;
verses.38:16: and their lamp-cups that are upon the ends, nut-shaped, out of them; and the sockets out of them, so that the lamps might be upon them, and the seventh socket from the end of the lamp-cup upon the top above, wholly solid, of gold;
verses.38:17: and seven golden lamps upon it, and its tongs of gold, and their oil vessels of gold.
verses.38:18: He overlaid the pillars with silver, and cast golden rings for the pillar, and gilded the bars with gold, and overlaid the pillars of the veil with gold, and made the hooks of gold.
verses.38:19: He also made the clasps of the tabernacle of gold, and the clasps of the court and clasps for stretching out the covering above, of bronze.
verses.38:20: He cast the silver capitals of the tabernacle, and the bronze capitals of the door of the tabernacle, and the gate of the court; and he made silver hooks for the pillars upon the pillars; he overlaid them with silver.
verses.38:21: He also made the pegs of the court of bronze.
verses.38:22: He made the bronze altar out of the bronze censers that belonged to the men who rebelled with the congregation of Korah.
verses.38:23: He made all the utensils of the altar, its firepan, and the base, and the basins, and the flesh-hooks of bronze.
verses.38:24: He made for the altar a grating, a work of network, beneath the firepan, under it up to the middle of it; and he placed upon it four bronze rings on the four sides of the grating of the altar, wide for the bars, so as to carry the altar with them.
verses.38:25: He made the holy anointing oil and the composition of the incense, the pure work of a perfumer.
verses.38:26: He made the bronze laver and its bronze base from the mirrors of the women who fasted, who fasted by the doors of the tabernacle of testimony on the day that he pitched it;
verses.38:27: and he made the laver so that Moses and Aaron and his sons might wash their hands and feet from it when they entered into the tabernacle of testimony; or whenever they drew near to the altar to minister, they washed from it, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
verses.39:1: All the gold that was worked for the tasks according to all the workmanship of the sanctuary was of the gold of the firstfruits offering: twenty-nine talents and seven hundred and twenty shekels, according to the holy shekel.
verses.39:2: And the offering of silver from the numbered men of the congregation was one hundred talents and one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels; one drachma per head, half of a shekel, according to the holy shekel.
verses.39:3: Everyone who passed through the numbering, from twenty years old and upward, amounted to six hundred thousand, and three thousand five hundred and fifty.
verses.39:4: And the one hundred talents of silver were for the casting of the one hundred capitals of the tabernacle and for the one hundred capitals of the veil, one hundred capitals to the one hundred talents, a talent to each capital.
verses.39:5: And the one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels they made into the hooks for the pillars, and he overlaid their capitals with gold and adorned them.
verses.39:6: And the bronze of the offering was seventy talents and one thousand five hundred shekels.
verses.39:7: And from them he made the bases of the door of the tabernacle of testimony,
verses.39:8: and the bases of the gate all around, and the bases of the gate of the court, and the pegs of the tabernacle, and the pegs of the court all around,
verses.39:9: and the bronze grating of the altar, and all the utensils of the altar, and all the implements of the tabernacle of testimony.
verses.39:10: And the children of Israel did just as the Lord commanded Moses; so they did.
verses.39:11: And the remaining gold of the offering they made into vessels to minister with them before the Lord;
verses.39:12: and the blue, and purple, and scarlet that were left over they made into garments of ministry for Aaron, so as to minister in them in the sanctuary.
verses.39:13: And they brought the garments to Moses, and the tabernacle and its utensils, and the bases, and its bars, and the pillars,
verses.39:15: and the altar and all its utensils, and the anointing oil, and the compounded incense, and the pure lampstand,
verses.39:16: and its lamps, the lamps for burning, and the oil for the light,
verses.39:17: and the table of showbread and all its utensils, and the loaves set forth,
verses.39:18: and the garments of the sanctuary that belong to Aaron, and the garments of his sons for the priesthood,
verses.39:19: and the hangings of the court and the pillars, and the veil of the door of the tabernacle and of the gate of the court,
verses.39:20: and all the utensils of the tabernacle and all its implements, and the hides, rams' skins dyed red, and the coverings, blue skins, and the coverings of the remaining things, and the pegs and all the implements for the works of the tabernacle of testimony.
verses.39:22: That which the Lord commanded Moses, so the children of Israel made all the equipment.
verses.39:23: And Moses saw all the works, and they had done them; in the manner that the Lord commanded Moses, so they did them; and Moses blessed them.
verses.40:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.40:2: "On the first day of the first month, at the new moon, you shall set up the tabernacle of testimony.
verses.40:3: And you shall cover the ark of testimony with the veil.
verses.40:4: And you shall bring in the table and set out its presentation; and you shall bring in the lampstand and place its lamps.
verses.40:5: And you shall set the golden altar for burning incense before the ark, and you shall place a covering of the veil over the door of the tabernacle of testimony.
verses.40:6: And the altar of burnt offerings you shall set beside the doors of the tabernacle of testimony.
verses.40:8: And you shall enclose the tabernacle, and you shall sanctify all that belongs to it all around; and you shall anoint the altar of burnt offerings and all its vessels.
verses.40:9: And you shall take the anointing oil and anoint the tabernacle and all that is in it, and you shall sanctify it and all its vessels, and it shall be holy.
verses.40:10: And you shall sanctify the altar, and it shall be most holy.
verses.40:12: And you shall bring Aaron and his sons to the doors of the tabernacle of testimony, and wash them with water.
verses.40:13: And you shall clothe Aaron with the holy garments, and anoint him and sanctify him to serve as priest to Me.
verses.40:14: And you shall bring his sons forward and clothe them with tunics,
verses.40:15: and you shall anoint them just as you anointed their father, and they shall serve as priests to Me; and it shall come to pass that an anointing of priesthood shall belong to them forever, throughout their generations."
verses.40:16: And Moses did all that the Lord commanded him; so he did.
verses.40:17: And it came to pass in the first month, in the second year of their going out from Egypt, at the new moon, that the tabernacle was set up.
verses.40:18: And Moses set up the tabernacle, and placed the capitals, and inserted the bars, and set up the pillars.
verses.40:19: And he spread out the curtains over the tabernacle, and placed the covering of the tabernacle upon it from above, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
verses.40:20: And taking the testimonies, he put them into the ark, and placed the poles beneath the ark,
verses.40:21: and he brought the ark into the tabernacle, and placed the covering of the veil, and covered the ark of testimony, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
verses.40:22: And he placed the table in the tabernacle of testimony, on the north side of the tabernacle of testimony, outside the veil of the tabernacle,
verses.40:23: and he set out upon it loaves of presentation before the Lord, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
verses.40:24: And he put the lampstand in the tabernacle of testimony, on the south side of the tabernacle,
verses.40:25: and he placed its lamps before the Lord, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
verses.40:26: And he put the golden altar in the tabernacle of testimony opposite the veil,
verses.40:27: and he offered upon it the compounded incense, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
verses.40:29: And the altar of burnt offerings he set beside the doors of the tabernacle,
verses.40:33: and he set up the court all around the tabernacle and the altar; and Moses finished all the works.
verses.40:34: And the cloud covered the tabernacle of testimony, and the tabernacle was filled with the glory of the Lord.
verses.40:35: And Moses was not able to enter into the tabernacle of testimony, because the cloud overshadowed it, and the tabernacle was filled with the glory of the Lord.
verses.40:36: Now whenever the cloud ascended from the tabernacle, the sons of Israel would break camp with their baggage;
verses.40:37: but if the cloud did not ascend, they would not break camp until the day on which the cloud ascended.
verses.40:38: For a cloud was upon the tabernacle by day, and fire was upon it by night, in the sight of all Israel, throughout all their journeys.

notes.1:5: The Septuagint counts seventy-five souls descending from Jacob (compare Acts 7:14), whereas the Masoretic Text reads seventy.
notes.1:11: The Septuagint adds "and On, which is Heliopolis" as a third fortified city alongside Pithom and Raamses.
notes.1:21: The Septuagint uses a third-person plural verb ("they made houses for themselves"), whereas the Masoretic Text states that God established households for the midwives.
notes.2:2: Here and in verse 3, the Septuagint uses plural verbs ("seeing... they hid... they could no longer hide"), including both parents (compare Hebrews 11:23), whereas the Masoretic Text uses singular verbs referring to Moses's mother.
notes.2:16: The Septuagint explicitly names the priest of Midian "Jethro" twice in this verse, while verse 18 refers to him as "Reuel."
notes.2:25: The Septuagint renders the final clause as a passive ("and He was made known to them"), whereas the Masoretic Text reads "and God knew."
notes.3:4: The Septuagint renders Moses's response as "What is it?" rather than "Here I am."
notes.3:8: Here and in verse 17, the Septuagint lists seven nations by including the Girgashites, whereas the Masoretic Text lists six.
notes.3:14: The Septuagint translates God's self-revelation using the masculine present participle "ho on" ("He who is" or "the Existing One"), expressing His eternal, self-existent being.
notes.3:17: The Septuagint reads the third person ("And He said"), continuing Moses's quotation of God to the elders, whereas the Masoretic Text reads the first person ("And I said").
notes.4:6: The Greek text reads simply "like snow" (ὡσεὶ χιών), without the mention of leprosy found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.4:16: The Greek "in the things pertaining to God" (τὰ πρὸς τὸν θεόν) clarifies the Hebrew idiom "as God," emphasizing Moses' role as mediator of God's word to Aaron.
notes.4:24: The Greek attributes this encounter to "an angel of the Lord" (ἄγγελος Κυρίου), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text names the Lord directly.
notes.4:25: Instead of the Hebrew "bridegroom of blood," the Greek renders Zipporah's words as "The blood of the circumcision of my child has ceased" (ἔστη τὸ αἷμα τῆς περιτομῆς τοῦ παιδίου μου), explaining why the angel withdrew in verse 26.
notes.5:3: The Greek reads "has summoned us" (προσκέκληται ἡμᾶς) rather than "has met with us," and renders the threatened judgments as "death or slaughter" (θάνατος ἢ φόνος).
notes.5:14: The phrase "yesterday and the third day" (ἐχθὲς καὶ τρίτην ἡμέραν, also in 4:10 and 5:7) preserves the Septuagint's literal rendering of the Hebrew idiom for "previously."
notes.5:16: Where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "the fault is with your own people," the Greek translates the clause as an active future verb: "You will therefore wrong your own people" (ἀδικήσεις οὖν τὸν λαόν σου).
notes.6:3: The Septuagint reads "being their God" here rather than the Masoretic "as God Almighty."
notes.6:12: The Greek renders the Hebrew idiom "uncircumcised of lips" interpretively as "lacking in speech" (alogos) here and "faltering of speech" (ischnophonos) in 6:30.
notes.6:15: The Septuagint identifies Shaul's mother as "the Phoenician woman" rather than the Masoretic "Canaanite woman."
notes.6:18: The Septuagint lists Kohath's second son as Issachar here (compare Izhar in 6:21) and gives Kohath's lifespan as one hundred and thirty years (Masoretic Text: one hundred and thirty-three).
notes.6:20: The Septuagint identifies Jochebed as Amram's cousin ("the daughter of his father's brother" rather than his aunt), includes Miriam among her children, and records Amram's lifespan as one hundred and thirty-two years (Masoretic Text: one hundred and thirty-seven).
notes.7:9: The Septuagint uses "dragon" (drakon) here and in 7:10 and 7:12, distinguishing it from "serpent" (ophis) in 7:15.
notes.7:13: The Septuagint reads "just as the Lord had commanded them" where the Masoretic Text has "just as the Lord had spoken."
notes.7:19: The final clause shifts to a past-tense narrative verb ("And there was blood") in the Septuagint, whereas the Masoretic Text continues the Lord's future-tense command.
notes.7:26: Verses 7:26-29 in the Septuagint correspond to 8:1-4 in the Masoretic Text and most English translations.
notes.8:2: The Greek preserves both the plural "brought up the frogs" and a collective singular passive clause "and the frog was brought up," a distinctive Septuagint reading.
notes.8:11: Greek uses the verb barynō ("become heavy" / "make heavy") here and in 8:28, 9:7, and 9:34, distinct from sklērynō ("harden") in 8:15, 9:12, and 9:35; here the Septuagint uses the passive "his heart became heavy."
notes.8:17: Greek kynomyia ("dog-fly") is the Septuagint's specific rendering of the fourth plague as a biting fly, used as a collective singular throughout verses 17–27.
notes.8:18: "Goshen" renders the Greek form Gesem; the Septuagint also concludes with the distinctive declaration "the Lord, the Lord of all the earth."
notes.9:14: Greek synantēmata ("afflictions"), literally "encounters" or "visitations," denotes the calamities sent by the Lord upon Pharaoh and Egypt.
notes.9:15: The Septuagint employs direct future verbs ("I will strike... put to death... you shall be blotted out"), expressing an imminent warning of judgment rather than a past counterfactual condition.
notes.9:17: Greek enpoiē ("lay claim to") means to assert ownership or hold onto, reflecting the Septuagint's distinctive wording in this rebuke.
notes.9:23: Greek phōnai ("thunderings"), literally "voices" or "sounds," is used throughout verses 23–34 for peals of thunder, including "thunderings of God" in 9:28.
notes.10:1: The Greek reads "in succession" (hexes) and "upon them," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "these signs of Mine in his midst."
notes.10:7: The Greek uses the neuter "this" (touto) for the "stumbling block" (skolon) and asks "Or do you wish to know that Egypt has perished?" rather than the Hebrew "Do you not yet know?"
notes.10:13: The Greek specifies "a south wind" (anemon noton) rather than an east wind, has Moses lift his staff "toward heaven," and omits an explicit subject "the Lord" before "brought."
notes.10:22: The Greek intensifies the plague with an asyndetic triad—"darkness, gloom, and tempest" (skotos gnophos thyella)—and in 10:23 specifies that no one rose "from his bed."
notes.11:2: The Greek adds "secretly" (kryphe) and "clothing" (himatismon) to the command, while omitting the separate clause about women asking their neighbors.
notes.11:3: The Greek adds "and they lent to them" (kai echresan autois) and lists three groups before whom Moses became great: the Egyptians, Pharaoh, and all his servants.
notes.11:7: The Greek verb paradoxazei denotes making a wondrous distinction, and "that you may see" (ides) is second-person singular rather than the Hebrew plural "that you may know."
notes.11:9: The Greek uses an emphatic first-person active idiom ("that I may exceedingly multiply My signs and My wonders"), whereas the Hebrew has a passive verb ("that My wonders may be multiplied").
notes.12:10: The Greek text includes the clause "and a bone shall not be broken from it" (absent from the Masoretic Text here, though present in 12:46), and uses middle/passive verb forms that may also reflect orthographic variation for second-person plural imperatives.
notes.12:13: Here (and in 12:27) the Septuagint renders the Passover verb with Greek skepazo ("shelter, cover, protect"), whereas in 12:23 it uses parerchomai ("pass over" or "pass by").
notes.12:19: Greek giorais ("sojourners") is a rare Septuagint transliteration of the Aramaic word for a resident alien or proselyte.
notes.12:22: The Septuagint reads para ten thyran ("beside the door") twice, interpreting the Hebrew word saph as "threshold/doorway" rather than "basin."
notes.12:40: The Septuagint specifies that the dwelling was "in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan," and this Greek text (following Codex Vaticanus) gives the duration as "four hundred and thirty-five years" here and in 12:41 rather than four hundred and thirty.
notes.13:4: The Greek renders the Hebrew month name Abib descriptively as "the month of the new crops" (en mēni tōn neōn), referring to the spring harvest of fresh grain.
notes.13:5: The Greek text lists all seven nations of Canaan, including the Girgashites and Perizzites, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text names five here.
notes.13:6: The Greek reads "Six days" for eating unleavened bread prior to the seventh-day feast, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Seven days."
notes.13:13: The Greek commands "you shall redeem it" (lytrōsē auto) if a firstborn donkey is not exchanged, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text commands breaking its neck.
notes.13:18: The Greek reads "in the fifth generation" (pemptē de genea), interpreting the underlying Hebrew term from the root for "five" rather than "armed" or "in battle array."
notes.14:2: The Greek translates the Hebrew place name Pi-hahiroth as a common noun, "the farmstead" (tēs epauleōs), here and in verse nine.
notes.14:10: The Greek states that the Egyptians "had encamped" (estratopedeusan) behind Israel, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text describes them marching after Israel.
notes.14:20: The Greek reads "there came darkness and gloom, and the night passed," differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which states that the cloud gave light to the night.
notes.14:21: The Greek specifies a "south wind" (anemō notō), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text specifies an "east wind."
notes.14:25: The Greek reads that the Lord "bound fast the axles of their chariots" (synedēsen tous axonas), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text speaks of removing or clogging their chariot wheels.
notes.15:3: The Greek text describes the Lord as "the One who shatters wars" (literally "crushing wars"), a distinctive Septuagint rendering compared to the Hebrew "man of war."
notes.15:13: The Greek reads "in Your righteousness" and uses a verb meaning "summoned" or "encouraged," preserving the Septuagint wording rather than the Hebrew "in Your steadfast love" and "You guided."
notes.15:23: The Greek translates the name of the site directly as Pikria ("Bitterness"), explaining the bitter waters of Marah (Greek Merra).
notes.16:23: The Greek text explicitly names "the Lord" as the speaker and casts the opening clause as a rhetorical question ("Is this not the word that the Lord spoke?"), whereas the Hebrew has Moses speaking declaratively.
notes.16:33: The Greek specifies "one golden jar" (a detail echoed in Hebrews 9:4), whereas the Hebrew text mentions a jar without specifying gold.
notes.16:35: The Greek reads "a region of Phoenicia" where the Hebrew reads "the border of the land of Canaan," reflecting Hellenistic Septuagint geographical terminology.
notes.16:36: The Greek transliterates the dry measure as gomor (here rendered "omer") and defines it as "the tenth part of the three measures," corresponding to the Hebrew ephah of three seahs.
notes.17:7: The Septuagint translates the place names into Greek as Peirasmos ("Testing") and Loidoresis ("Reviling"), corresponding to Hebrew Massah and Meribah.
notes.17:9: The Greek text uses Iesous, the standard Septuagint form of the name Joshua, and specifies "mighty men" (andras dynatous) where the Masoretic Text reads simply "men."
notes.17:15: The Septuagint names the altar "The Lord Is My Refuge" (Kyrios kataphyge mou), whereas the Masoretic Text reads "The Lord Is My Banner."
notes.17:16: The Septuagint reads "with a hidden hand" (en cheiri kryphaia), differing from the Masoretic Text's difficult phrase usually rendered "a hand upon the throne of the Lord."
notes.18:9: The Septuagint reads "was amazed" (exeste), whereas the Masoretic Text reads "rejoiced."
notes.18:13: The Greek phrase meta ten epaurion literally means "after the next day," a hyper-literal rendering of the Hebrew idiom for "on the next day."
notes.18:21: The Septuagint specifies "righteous men, hating arrogance" (andras dikaious, misountas hyperephanian), whereas the Masoretic Text has "men of truth, hating dishonest gain."
notes.18:23: The Septuagint reads "God shall strengthen you" (katischysei se ho theos), where the Masoretic Text reads "and God so commands you."
notes.19:3: The Septuagint states that God called Moses "out of heaven" (ek tou ouranou), whereas the Masoretic Text reads "from the mountain."
notes.19:6: The Septuagint renders the covenant title "a royal priesthood" (basileion hierateuma, later echoed in 1 Peter 2:9), where the Masoretic Text reads "a kingdom of priests."
notes.19:9: The Septuagint reads "in a pillar of cloud" (en stylo nepheles), whereas the Masoretic Text reads "in a thick cloud."
notes.19:13: The Septuagint specifies that the people may ascend "when the sounds and the trumpets and the cloud depart from the mountain," differing from the Masoretic Text's "when the ram's horn sounds long."
notes.19:18: The Septuagint reads "all the people were exceedingly astounded" (exeste pas ho laos sphodra), whereas the Masoretic Text reads "the whole mountain trembled greatly."
notes.20:11: The Greek text omits the sea from the summary of creation and states that the Lord blessed the seventh day rather than the Sabbath day, differing from the Masoretic Hebrew.
notes.20:13: The Septuagint orders verses 13 through 15 as adultery, theft, and murder, whereas the Masoretic Hebrew places them in the order murder, adultery, and theft.
notes.20:17: The Greek text places coveting a neighbor's wife before coveting his house and adds his field to the list.
notes.20:18: The Greek literally says the people saw the voice and the torches (or flashes), expressing the thunder and lightning of Sinai in vivid visual terms.
notes.21:6: The Greek interprets the Hebrew term for God or judges specifically as the judgment seat (tribunal) of God.
notes.21:16: The Septuagint places the statute on reviling parents in verse 16 and the statute on kidnapping in verse 17, reversing the Masoretic sequence.
notes.21:22: In verses 22 and 23, the Septuagint distinguishes between a child not yet formed and one already formed, whereas the Masoretic Hebrew focuses on whether further harm follows.
notes.21:29: Literally "before yesterday and before the third day," a Septuagint idiom for "in times past" (likewise in verse 36).
notes.21:37: This verse concludes chapter 21 in the Septuagint, whereas in the Masoretic Text and most English Bibles it is numbered as Exodus 22:1.
notes.22:2: The Greek reads 'he shall die in return' (antapothaneitai), imposing capital liability on one who kills a thief after sunrise, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text speaks of making restitution.
notes.22:4: The Septuagint preserves a two-part distinction not found in the Masoretic Text: partial grazing requires restitution according to the field's yield, whereas grazing an entire field requires restitution from the best of one's field and vineyard.
notes.22:12: The Greek reads 'he shall bring him to the prey' (axei auton epi ten theran), referring to leading the owner to the torn carcass rather than bringing remains as evidence as in the Masoretic Text.
notes.22:27: The Septuagint renders the Hebrew plural 'elohim' explicitly as plural 'gods' (theous) alongside plural 'rulers' (archontas), where other traditions render 'God' or 'judges.'
notes.23:7: The Greek addresses the judge directly ('you shall not justify the ungodly for the sake of bribes'), whereas the Masoretic Text has a first-person divine declaration ('for I will not acquit the wicked').
notes.23:18: The Septuagint opens with a clause echoing Exodus 34:24 ('For when I cast out nations... and enlarge your borders') and reads 'My incense-offering' (thymiamatos mou) where the Hebrew has 'My sacrifice.'
notes.23:19: The Greek specifies 'a lamb' (arna), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text specifies a young goat.
notes.23:22: The first half of this verse in the Septuagint contains an expanded covenant promise closely paralleling Exodus 19:5-6 before resuming the promise of divine aid against Israel's enemies.
notes.24:1: The Septuagint reads a third-person plural future, "they shall worship," rather than a second-person command, and transcribes Abihu as Greek Abioud (here rendered by the standard English name Abihu).
notes.24:10: The Septuagint reads "the place where the God of Israel stood" rather than directly saying they saw God, softening the anthropomorphism of the Hebrew text.
notes.24:11: The Septuagint translates "not even one perished" (Greek diephonesen) and "they appeared in the place of God," continuing the reverent phrasing of verse 10.
notes.25:5: The Septuagint renders Hebrew acacia wood as "incorruptible wood" (xyla asepta) and tahash skins as "blue-dyed skins"; verse 6 of the Hebrew text (listing oil and spices) is omitted in the Septuagint here.
notes.25:22: The Septuagint reads "I will make Myself known to you" (gnosthesomai), reflecting a reading of the Hebrew verb from the root "to know" rather than "to meet."
notes.25:23: The Septuagint describes "a golden table of pure gold" rather than a wooden table overlaid with gold, and accordingly omits the instruction to overlay it in verse 24.
notes.25:35: The Septuagint reads "under the four branches" (rather than repeating "under the two branches") and repeats the clause regarding the four nut-shaped cups on the lampstand from verse 34.
notes.26:12: The Septuagint omits the Hebrew Masoretic Text's mention of the remaining half curtain, stating simply that the excess of the curtains is placed beneath to cover the rear of the tabernacle.
notes.26:14: The Septuagint renders the outermost covering as "blue skins" (dermata hyakinthina), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text uses the debated term tachash (often translated as badger, sea cow, or fine leather).
notes.26:15: Throughout Exodus 26 and 27, the Septuagint renders Hebrew shittim (acacia) wood as "incorruptible wood" (xyla asepta) and refers to the tabernacle's vertical frames as "pillars" (styloi).
notes.26:18: The Septuagint reverses the north-south order relative to the Hebrew Masoretic Text, specifying the first twenty pillars on the north side (v. 18) and the second twenty on the south side (v. 20).
notes.26:34: Where the Hebrew Masoretic Text commands placing the mercy seat upon the ark, the Septuagint instructs that the ark of the testimony in the Holy of Holies be concealed with the veil.
notes.27:3: The Septuagint specifies a "rim" (stephane) and "cover" (kalypter) for the altar, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text lists pots for ashes and shovels.
notes.27:9: In verses 9–13, the Septuagint orients the court's sides differently from the Masoretic Text, placing the two hundred-cubit sides toward the southwest (lips) and east (apeliotes), and the two fifty-cubit sides toward the sea (west) and south (notos).
notes.27:14: In verses 14–16, the Septuagint refers to "the height" (to hypsos) of the gate hangings as fifteen and twenty cubits, whereas verse 18 states the court's height as five cubits (in the Masoretic Text, fifteen and twenty cubits are horizontal widths).
notes.27:18: The Septuagint reads "one hundred by one hundred" for the length of the court, paralleling "fifty by fifty" for the width, where the Masoretic Text has "one hundred cubits."
notes.28:11: In the Greek text, the clause bridges verses 11 and 12 without the additional gold-setting instructions found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.28:15: Greek logion ('oracle') presents the breastpiece as an instrument of divine revelation; the sentence continues across the verse boundary into verse 16.
notes.28:29: The Greek text omits verses 23 through 28 of the Hebrew numbering and summarizes the attachment of the chainwork and small shields at the end of verse 29.
notes.28:30: Greek 'the Manifestation and the Truth' (delosis and aletheia) interprets the Hebrew Urim and Thummim conceptually rather than transliterating them.
notes.28:36: Greek hagiasma Kyriou uses the genitive ('Holiness of the Lord'), corresponding to 'Holiness to the Lord' in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.29:5: The Greek text adds 'your brother' and renders the high priest's vestments distinctly as the 'full-length tunic' (chitona ton podere), the 'shoulder-piece' (epomida, corresponding to the Hebrew ephod), and the 'oracle' (logion, corresponding to the breastpiece).
notes.29:20: The Septuagint applies blood to Aaron's right ear, the tip (akron) of his right hand, and the tip of his right foot before his sons, and places the pouring of the ram's blood around the altar at the end of verse 21.
notes.29:24: The Greek renders the ritual presentation terms as 'separated offering' (aphorisma, vv. 24, 26-28, corresponding to the Hebrew wave offering), 'contribution' (aphairema, vv. 27-28, corresponding to the heave offering), and 'sacrifices of deliverance' (thymata soterion, v. 28).
notes.29:43: The Septuagint preserves distinctive readings in verses 43 and 45-46: 'I will give orders' (taxomai), the first-person 'I will be sanctified in My glory' (hagiasthēsomai), and 'be called upon' (epiklēthēsomai/epiklēthēnai) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'meet,' 'it shall be sanctified,' and 'dwell.'
notes.30:6: The Greek reads 'the ark of the testimonies' (plural) and omits the Hebrew clause referring to the mercy seat over the testimony.
notes.30:13: The Greek renders the sanctuary weights with Hellenistic coinage terms, 'didrachma' and 'obols,' rather than the Hebrew 'shekel' and 'gerahs.'
notes.30:24: The Greek specifies 'iris' (ireos), whereas the Hebrew text lists cassia.
notes.30:27: The Greek repeats 'the tabernacle of testimony and all its vessels' here and lists the table in verse 28, where it also omits the base of the laver.
notes.31:3: The Greek reads 'a divine spirit' (pneuma theion) rather than the Hebrew 'the Spirit of God.'
notes.31:4: The Greek adds 'and in blue and purple and spun scarlet,' a textile clause absent from the Hebrew text.
notes.31:6: The Greek names Bezalel's co-worker 'Eliab,' whereas the Hebrew text reads 'Oholiab.'
notes.31:8: The Greek groups both altars together as 'the altars' here and has a shorter verse 9 naming only the laver and its base.
notes.32:4: The Greek uses a singular verb ("and he said"), attributing the declaration directly to Aaron, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads a plural ("and they said").
notes.32:8: In the Septuagint text, verse 9 of the Hebrew numbering (where the Lord calls Israel a stiff-necked people) is not present, and verse 8 reads "which you commanded them" rather than "which I commanded them."
notes.32:14: The Greek reads "was appeased, so as to preserve His people," whereas the Hebrew states that the Lord relented from the harm He had spoken of doing to His people.
notes.32:18: The Greek reads "leading a song of wine," highlighting drunken revelry in the camp, whereas the Hebrew reads simply "singing."
notes.33:2: The Greek reads "you shall drive out" (second-person singular) and lists six nations, including the Girgashite and omitting the Canaanite found in the Hebrew text.
notes.33:5: The Greek addresses the sons of Israel directly and warns "lest I bring another plague upon you" and "I will show you what I will do to you," differing from the Hebrew ("in a single moment" and "that I may know").
notes.33:11: "Nave" preserves the distinct Septuagint proper name (Naue) where the Hebrew text has "Nun."
notes.33:18: The Greek reads "Manifest Yourself to me" (echoing 33:13) rather than "Show me Your glory" as in the Hebrew; in 33:19 the Greek likewise reads "in My glory" where the Hebrew has "all My goodness."
notes.34:11: The Septuagint lists seven nations here, adding the Girgashite, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text lists six.
notes.34:18: The Greek phrase "month of new produce" (literally "of the new things") is the Septuagint's rendering of the Hebrew month name Abib.
notes.34:20: Where the Hebrew Masoretic Text commands breaking the neck of an unredeemed donkey, the Septuagint specifies paying a price ("you shall pay a price").
notes.34:26: The Septuagint reads "offer a lamb" rather than the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "boil a young goat."
notes.34:29: The Septuagint renders the radiance of Moses' face as "the appearance of the skin of his face had been glorified," vocabulary later echoed in 2 Corinthians 3:7-13.
notes.35:7: The Septuagint consistently renders the Hebrew coverings and acacia wood as "blue-dyed skins" and "incorruptible wood."
notes.35:9: The Septuagint's shorter tabernacle summary omits verses 8, 15, 17, and 18 of the Masoretic numbering, and here reads "sardius stones," "stones for engraving," and "the full-length robe."
notes.35:22: The Greek reads "the men brought from the women," differing from the Hebrew phrasing "men as well as women."
notes.35:27: The Greek word rendered "oracle" is the Septuagint's standard term for the high priest's breastpiece of judgment.
notes.35:34: The Septuagint preserves the distinct proper name "Eliab" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "Oholiab."
notes.36:1: The Greek text reads Eliab, corresponding to Oholiab in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.36:8: Beginning here, the Septuagint departs from the order of the Hebrew Masoretic Text, placing the construction of the priestly garments in 36:8–38 (corresponding to Hebrew Exodus 39:1–31).
notes.36:15: Greek logion literally means "oracle," the Septuagint's regular rendering for the high priest's breastpiece.
notes.36:24: The Greek clause eis tas lacks an explicit noun before "the two braided cords" in the manuscript tradition; "the ends" is supplied from the preceding verse to complete the sense.
notes.37:1: In the Septuagint arrangement, chapter 37 recounts the tabernacle curtains, veils, and courtyard (corresponding to parts of Hebrew Exodus 36 and 38), while the ark and furnishings follow in chapter 38.
notes.37:4: Greek aseptos literally means "incorruptible" or "imperishable," the Septuagint's standard designation for acacia wood.
notes.37:7: The Septuagint states the court's measurement as "one hundred by one hundred" (here and in verse 9) and names both the southwest (lips) and the south (notos) in addition to the north, sea (west), and east.
notes.37:13: The Greek text reads "one hundred and fifty cubits," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "fifteen cubits."
notes.38:18: Verses 18–26 shift from the connecting phrase "And he" to an emphatic demonstrative pronoun (houtos, literally "this man"), highlighting Bezalel's craftsmanship across these furnishings.
notes.38:20: The Septuagint renders the tabernacle sockets or bases as "capitals" (kephalidas), a distinctive architectural term carried through into 39:4–5.
notes.38:22: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text, the Septuagint explicitly states that the bronze altar was made from the censers of the men who rebelled with Korah (compare Numbers 16:36–40).
notes.38:26: The Greek reads "the women who fasted, who fasted," preserving a distinctive Septuagint reading in place of the Hebrew "women who served."
notes.39:1: The Septuagint specifies "seven hundred and twenty shekels," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads seven hundred and thirty shekels.
notes.39:4: The Greek explicitly reads "one hundred capitals of the veil," a distinctive Septuagint reading where the Hebrew Masoretic Text specifies four sockets for the veil.
notes.39:6: The Septuagint gives "one thousand five hundred shekels" of bronze here, differing from the two thousand four hundred shekels in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.39:13: Because the Septuagint arranges the tabernacle construction account differently from the Hebrew Masoretic Text, standard LXX versification skips numbers 14 and 21 in this chapter.
notes.40:8: The Septuagint omits verses 7 and 11 (concerning the washbasin) and places the command to anoint the altar of burnt offerings here rather than in verse 10, while reading "enclose the tabernacle" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text refers to setting up the court.
notes.40:17: The Greek text adds "of their going out from Egypt" and specifies "at the new moon," expanding on the date formula in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.40:18: The Greek reads "placed the capitals" (the tops of the pillars), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text mentions laying the bases and setting up the frames.
notes.40:33: The Septuagint omits verses 28 and 30–32 (concerning the entrance screen and the bronze basin) and uses the plural "all the works" for Moses' completion of the sanctuary.
notes.40:38: The Greek reads "a cloud" (rather than "the cloud of the Lord") and states that fire was "upon it" (the tabernacle) by night, rather than "in it" (the cloud) as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
